options: Tests by persons within the same project team but not directly involved in the development of the system
Tests by persons from a different company or organization
Tests by the person who wrote the code
Tests by a person who identified the defect
explanation: d) is correct (NOT a level of independence). Work products can be tested by their author (no independence), by the author's peers from the same team (some independence), by testers from outside the author's team but within the organization (high independence), or by testers from outside the organization (very high independence).

stem: In a self-organizing agile team, who is primarily responsible for deciding how to communicate test status?
options: The project manager
The test manager
The stakeholders
The team itself
explanation: d) is correct. Self-organizing teams are empowered to make decisions about their work, including communication.

stem:
Consider the following state transition diagram for a credit-card only, unattended gasoline pump

Assume further that each test must start at the beginning state, waiting for customer, and each test ends when a transition arrives at the beginning state.

What is the MINIMAL number of test cases to achieve valid transitions coverage?
explanation:
c) is correct. Each transition must be traversed at least once. To do so you need six (6) tests:

  • TC1: Can cover the happy path, a successful purchase

  • TC2: Cancels from waiting for fuel type

  • TC3: Timeout from waiting for fuel type

  • TC4: Cancels from waiting for pumping

  • TC5: Timeout from waiting for pumping

  • TC6: The insertion of an invalid credit card

While the order is immaterial, fewer than six tests fail to cover one of the transitions inbound to waiting for customer or violates the rules about where a test starts or ends. More than six tests include tests that re-traverse already-covered transitions.

stem:
Which of the following best practices for achieving a "shift-left" approach are typically the responsibility of testers rather than developers?

  • i. TDD
  • ii. System testing
  • iii. Test system performance
  • iv. ATDD
  • v. Test component security
options: ii, iii, iv
ii, iv
ii, iii
ii, iii, iv, v
explanation:
c) is correct.

  • i. TDD – predominantly a developer-focused practice where developers write tests before they write the corresponding functionality

  • ii. System testing – may be performed by an independent test team

  • iii. Test System Performance – Performance testing (Quadrant Q4) is often a shared responsibility but typically leans more towards testers

  • iv. ATDD – Shared responsibility. The test cases are created by team members with different perspectives, e.g., customers, developers, and testers

  • v. Test Component Security – Component testing is normally performed by developers in their development environment

stem: A software testing team is conducting a multi-phase project where each phase needs to be tested individually and may require reverting to previous phases based on the outcomes of subsequent integration tests. Which practice allows the team to effectively manage different versions of test environments and associated documentation to ensure that each phase can be independently verified?
options: Issue management
Configuration management
Compliance management
Process management
explanation: b) is correct. Configuration management is ideally suited for this scenario as it involves the systematic handling of changes to the software project's configuration items, including test environments and documentation. It allows for precise control over different versions and states, enabling the team to revert to previous phases for independent verification when necessary.

stem: Which of the following best describes the main difference between static testing and dynamic testing?
options: Static testing finds defects directly, while dynamic testing causes failures from which the associated defects are determined through subsequent analysis
Static testing can be performed by developers, whereas testers only perform dynamic testing
Static testing is done after dynamic testing in the software development lifecycle
Dynamic testing can only be performed manually, while static testing can only be automated
explanation: a) is correct. Static testing and dynamic testing practices complement each other. They have similar objectives, such as supporting the detection of defects in work products, but there are also some differences, such as: Static testing finds defects directly, while dynamic testing causes failures from which the associated defects are determined through subsequent analysis.

stem: What testware is typically created as output from the test analysis activity?
options: Risk register and test conditions
Use cases, user manuals, and test conditions
Test conditions and coverage items
Test conditions and defect report
explanation:
d) is correct. Test analysis work products include: (prioritized) test conditions, and defect reports regarding defects in the test basis (if not fixed directly).

  • b) is not correct, an example of test basis rather than a testware

stem: Which of the following BEST defines EXIT criteria in a testing project?
options: All existing defects are found and fixed before release
Test progress metrics and product quality metrics are selected
Defect density is lower than two defects per KLOC
All user stories are estimated, and acceptance criteria are written
explanation: c) is correct. Exit criteria should be measurable and define when testing can be completed. A specific defect density threshold is a measurable exit criterion.

stem:
Your favorite bicycle daily rental store has just introduced a new Customer Relationship Management system and asked you, one of their most loyal members, to test it.

The implemented features are as follows:

  • Anyone can rent a bicycle, but members receive a 20% discount
  • However, if the return deadline is missed, the discount is no longer available
  • After 10 rentals, members get a gift: a T-Shirt
  • After 10 rentals, not a member gets a gift: One free rental

The decision table describing the implemented features looks as follows:

Based ONLY on the feature description of the Customer Relationship Management system, which of the following statements is true?
options: R1, R5, R6 can be merged into a single column
R7, R8 can be merged into a single column
R3 describes an impossible situation
R5, R6 can't be merged into a single column
explanation: b) is correct. R7 and R8 can be merged into a single column; it won't contradict any rules.

stem: Which of the following statements about BDD is true?
options: In BDD, tests are created based on acceptance criteria to drive the development of the related software
BDD tests belong to quadrant four (Q4) and are higher-level tests than system tests
BDD allows a developer to focus on testing the code based on the expected behavior of the software
The BDD process starts with a developer adding a test that captures the concept of the desired function of a small piece of code
explanation: c) is correct. BDD (Behavior-Driven Development) focuses on the expected behavior of the software, allowing developers to test code against that expected behavior.

stem: A tester is analyzing a program module with multiple nested 'if-else' statements. Which test technique would help ensure that all the possible paths through this module's logic are tested?
options: White-box test techniques
Black-box test techniques
Experience-based test techniques
Risk-based test techniques
explanation: a) is correct. White-box test techniques are based on an analysis of the internal structure of the code, making them suitable for testing all possible paths through nested if-else logic.

stem: Which of the following BEST describes how value is added by maintaining traceability between the test basis and test artifacts?
options: Maintenance testing can be fully automated based on changes to the initial requirements
It is possible to determine if a new test case has increased coverage of the requirements
Test managers can identify which testers found the highest severity defects
Areas that may be impacted by side-effects of a change can be targeted by confirmation testing
explanation: b) is correct. If all test cases are linked with requirements, then whenever a new test case (with traceability) is added, it is possible to see if any previously uncovered requirements are covered by the new test case.

stem:
Your team uses planning poker to estimate the test effort for a newly required feature.

Given the following user story: "As an online shopper, I want to easily select and manage delivery addresses during the checkout process, So I can ensure accurate and timely delivery of my purchased items"

  • Each estimator has a deck of cards with values similar to the shirt sizes ranging from extra-small to extra-extra-large (XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL)

During the first poker planning session, the following story points were given based on risk, effort, complexity, and proper extent of testing:

  • Product owner: M
  • Developers: XL
  • Testers: XXL

Which action should the team agree on?
options: As the developers are developing the system, the developer estimates should be taken as correct when there is a conflict

The team should hold a conversation to understand why the testers and product owner gave different story points for the work required for the story. Another round of the planning poker session should occur following that discussion
As the product owner owns the system, the customers' estimates should be taken as correct when there is a conflict
Another round of the planning poker session should occur following that discussion if consensus won't be reached user story won't be taken into the sprint backlog
explanation: b) is correct. The planning poker sessions should continue for the user story until the entire team is satisfied with the estimated effort.

stem: In order to maintain a high level of communication and ensure all team members are updated on the testing progress and issues in real-time, which type of tool should the tester advocate for?
options: Test management tools
Collaboration tools
DevOps tools
Containerization tools
explanation: b) is correct. Collaboration tools facilitate communication, which is needed to maintain a high level of communication and ensure all team members are updated in real-time.

stem:
You are preparing a test execution schedule for executing seven test cases TC 1 to TC 7.

The following figure includes the priorities of these test cases (1=highest priority, 3 = lowest priority).

The figure also shows the dependencies between test cases using arrows. For instance, the arrow from TC 4 to TC 5 means that TC 5 can only be executed if TC 4 was previously executed.

Which of the following is a possible test execution schedule that considers both priorities and dependencies?
options: TC3 - TC4 - TC7 - TC1 - TC2 - TC5 - TC6 - TC8
TC1 - TC3 - TC4 - TC7 - TC2 - TC5 - TC6 - TC8
TC3 - TC4 - TC7 - TC2 - TC5 - TC1 - TC6 - TC8
TC3 - TC2 - TC5 - TC6 - TC1 - TC8 - TC4 - TC7
explanation: c) is correct. TC7 and TC5 have the highest priority so those should be executed first. But TC7 has a dependency on TC4(2). And TC5 has a dependency on TC2(3). Both test cases have a dependency on TC3. Thus, the first TC to be executed will be TC3. As the number of test cases to be executed before TC5 and TC7 are equal, then we need to compare the priority of dependencies. TC4 has a higher priority than TC2. Thus it will be executed first. TC3 - TC4 - TC7 - TC2 - TC5. TC1 has higher priority than TC6. Thus the final order is: TC3 - TC4 - TC7 - TC2 - TC5 - TC1 - TC6 - TC8.

stem: Out of the following which is NOT a benefit of the "Whole Team Approach"?
options: Enhancing communication and collaboration within the team
Enabling the various skill sets within the team to be leveraged
Making quality everyone's responsibility
Specialized testers not required
explanation: d) is correct (NOT a benefit). Specialized testers are essentially required on agile projects.

stem: Which of the following is a good testing practice that applies to all software development lifecycles?
options: The importance of testing during the early stages of SDLC surpasses that of testing during later phases, primarily due to its capacity to identify more and higher priority defects
Different test levels have specific and different test objectives
All test levels have the same test objectives and goals
Performing detailed and comprehensive testing at lower levels makes testing at higher levels unnecessary
explanation: b) is correct. Each test level has specific and distinct test objectives, which is a good testing practice that applies to all SDLCs.

stem: During a code review, you notice a redundant conditional check that will always evaluate to the same result. This is an example of a defect that:
options: Would likely be found through both black-box and white-box testing
Would likely be found by white-box testing, but not black-box testing
Would likely be found by black-box testing, but not white-box testing
Would likely not be found by either black-box or white-box testing
explanation: b) is correct. White-box testing, with its focus on the internal code structure, is well-suited for identifying logical errors like unnecessary checks. Black-box testing might not reveal this if the functionality still works as expected based on input and output.

stem: Which review type explicitly is led by a moderator and has the main objective to make decisions regarding a technical problem?
options: Informal Review
Walkthrough
Technical Review
Inspection
explanation: c) is correct. A technical review is led by a moderator and explicitly aims to make decisions regarding technical problems. It also includes objectives such as gaining consensus, detecting anomalies, and evaluating quality, which aligns with the provided description.

stem: Which of the following test tasks is part of the main test activity 'test monitoring and control' in the testing process?
options: Propose improvements to the code review process so that developers merge fewer bugs into the master branch
Evaluating testability of the user stories and acceptance criteria
Give a higher priority to the 'Shopping cart' test suite as developers coded it faster than expected
Rewrite the description of the user story due to the change in the acceptance criteria
explanation: c) is correct. Test control uses the information from test monitoring to provide guidance and corrective actions, such as re-prioritizing tests when the situation changes.

stem: When would it be beneficial to combine error guessing with other test design techniques?
options: To provide comprehensive test coverage and mitigate the limitations of error guessing alone
When error guessing does not yield any relevant test ideas
To satisfy regulatory requirements that mandate specific testing methods
When the tester lacks sufficient experience to use black-box and white-box techniques
explanation: a) is correct. Combining error guessing with other techniques provides comprehensive test coverage and mitigates the limitations of error guessing alone.

stem: Which of the following statements about retrospectives is true?
options: Retrospectives are useful for identifying improvement opportunities, making users more satisfied with the product
With the help of a retrospective, you can quickly gather feedback on the latest release from business representatives
Thanks to retrospectives, developers, testers, and business representatives learn about problems and issues, which helps to avoid them in future iterations

One of the key values of retrospectives is prioritizing individuals and interactions over processes and tools. This emphasizes that if a process has a detrimental effect on team effectiveness, it should be eliminated
explanation: c) is correct. Retrospectives enable the team to learn from problems and issues encountered during the iteration, helping to avoid them in future iterations.

stem:
You received the following defect report from the developers stating that the anomaly described in this test report is not reproducible:

Id: BUG-0561 Defect: Spreadsheet formulas not calculating Date: 2023-March-12 – Emily Clarke – Open

The spreadsheet component of the suite fails to calculate any new formulas entered by the user. Repeated attempts to add simple formulas like SUM or AVERAGE result in blank cells instead of calculated results. This issue persists across several user accounts. No error messages displayed; however, the error log shows timeout issues when executing calculations. According to test case TC-2097, the application should process and display results immediately upon formula entry. This feature is integral to user operations as per REQ-0556. It is urgent and affects a critical business process.

The defect report does not have all the necessary details and you plan to add them. Which of the following items would NOT be typically included in a tester's initial defect report?
options: Any relevant database dumps, screenshots, or recordings
Steps to reproduce the issue
Expected results and actual results
Assignee field, by assigning a defect to a developer who does not have a ticket in progress
Identification of the test object and test environment
explanation:
d) is correct. Assigning a defect to a specific developer is typically not the tester's responsibility. This decision is usually made during the triage process, considering factors like expertise, workload, and priority. Assigning a defect prematurely can disrupt the workflow and create unnecessary bottlenecks. A defect report typically includes:

  • Unique identifier

  • Title with a short summary

  • Date when the anomaly was observed, issuing organization, and author, including their role

  • Identification of the test object and test environment

  • Context of the defect

  • Description of the failure

  • Expected results and actual results

  • Steps to reproduce

stem: A testing team defines the following objective: "To identify and fix defects in the new accounting software." Is this a valid test objective?
options: Yes, identifying and fixing defects improves software quality
Yes, this objective ensures all functionalities are thoroughly tested
No, fixing defects is part of the development process, not testing
No, this objective is too vague and lacks specific details
explanation:
c) is correct. The typical test objectives are:

  • Evaluating work products such as requirements, user stories, designs, and code

  • Triggering failures and finding defects

  • Ensuring required coverage of a test object

  • Reducing the level of risk of inadequate software quality

  • Verifying whether specified requirements have been fulfilled

  • Verifying that a test object complies with contractual, legal, and regulatory requirements

  • Providing information to stakeholders to allow them to make informed decisions

  • Building confidence in the quality of the test object

  • Validating whether the test object is complete and works as expected by the stakeholders

Fixing defects is part of debugging (development process), not testing.

stem: You are working as a tester in the team that follows the Iterative model. How does the choice of this software development lifecycle (SDLC) model impact the timing of testing?
options: Static testing can be performed at all test levels
Test analysis and design cannot be performed early in the SDLC
Dynamic testing can't be performed at all test levels
Acceptance testing can be performed at all test levels
explanation: d) is correct. In iterative models, testing is performed throughout the iteration, and acceptance testing can be performed at all test levels as feedback is gathered frequently from stakeholders.

stem:
Which of the following would NOT be considered an appropriate target for static testing?

  • i. A COTS project management software suite, without provided source code, utilized for organizing tasks and resources across multiple teams
  • ii. User manual documentation for a COTS accounting software used in the finance department
  • iii. Encrypted source code repositories safeguarding proprietary algorithms and intellectual property with secure access protocols
  • iv. UML state machine diagrams modeling system behavior
  • v. A Swagger document defining the RESTful API endpoints for a cloud-based service
options: i, ii
i, iii
i, ii, iii
i, ii, iii, iv
explanation: b) is correct. Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) software and services are built and delivered usually from a third party vendor. Work products that are not appropriate for static testing include those that are difficult to interpret by human beings and that should not be analyzed by tools (e.g., 3rd party executable code due to legal reasons). Encrypted code is too complex for humans and if it is properly encrypted it will not be analyzable by most tools.

stem: In which scenario would white-box test techniques NOT be applicable?
options: When the test cases need to be derived from the software's specified requirements and functionalities
When there is a need to ensure that every possible branch and path within the application code is executed
When optimizing the code and ensuring that all logical flows are adequately tested
When detailed code analysis is required to identify possible security vulnerabilities
explanation: a) is correct. White-box test techniques are based on an analysis of the internal structure of the code, not on specified requirements. Deriving test cases from specified requirements is the domain of black-box test techniques.

stem: Which of the following activities is NOT an example of what a tester would do during release planning?
options: Estimate test effort associated with user stories
Identify and refine functional and non-functional aspects of the test object
Determine the test approach
Plan the testing for the release
explanation: b) is correct. This is expected during iteration planning. Testers involved in release planning participate in writing testable user stories and acceptance criteria, participate in project and quality risk analyses, estimate test effort associated with user stories, determine the test approach, and plan the testing for the release.

stem: Which out of the following activities represent tasks and responsibilities that are consistent with the whole team approach in Agile projects?
options: Testers create user stories for the team
Testers are responsible for testing functional requirements, and developers are responsible for testing non-functional requirements
Every team member of the Agile team takes responsibility for testing tasks
Testers prioritize and estimate the user stories
explanation: c) is correct. The whole-team approach means that everyone on the team takes responsibility for testing tasks, not just the testers.

stem: What is a true statement regarding the relationship between statement coverage and defect detection?
options: Statement coverage ensures that all types of defects are detected
A higher percentage of statement coverage directly correlates to a lower number of defects in the code
Statement coverage can guarantee that every statement with a defect will be executed, but not necessarily reveal the defect
Achieving 100% statement coverage eliminates the need for further testing
explanation: c) is correct. When 100% statement coverage is achieved, it ensures that all executable statements in the code have been exercised at least once. In particular, this means that each statement with a defect will be executed, which may cause a failure demonstrating the presence of the defect. However, exercising a statement with a test case will not detect defects in all cases.

stem:
Can the following information be found in the test plan?

Product and project risks:

  • The critical functionality of the software may not work as expected under certain conditions, leading to a high-risk scenario
  • The user interface may not be intuitive, leading to potential user confusion and dissatisfaction
  • The software may not be compatible with certain browsers, operating systems, or third-party applications
  • Key team members may become unavailable due to unexpected circumstances, such as illness or unexpected departure
  • Delays in the delivery of external dependencies, such as third-party components or data, may affect the overall project schedule
options: Yes, product and project risks can be found in the context of testing
Yes, product and project risks can be found in the assumptions and constraints of the test project
Yes, product and project risks can be found in the risk register
No, project risks are part of the project policy rather than a test plan
explanation: c) is correct. The risk register is where product and project risks are documented, and it should be referenced in the test plan.

stem:
Consider the following definitions (1-6) and match the term (A-C) with the definition (1-6):

  1. Acceptance criteria are typically created based on the given/when/then format
  2. Tests are written first, then the code is written to satisfy the tests, and then the tests and code are refactored
  3. Derives tests from acceptance criteria as part of the system design process
  • A. Test-Driven Development (TDD)
  • B. Acceptance Test-Driven Development (ATDD)
  • C. Behavior-Driven Development (BDD)
explanation:
a) is correct.

    1. Given/when/then format → C. BDD
    1. Tests first, then code, then refactor → A. TDD
    1. Derives tests from acceptance criteria → B. ATDD

stem: Which of the following statements best describes why white-box testing may not detect defects of omission?
options: Because it focuses on testing the application from an external perspective without looking into the internal structures
Because it is primarily concerned with the validation of the user requirements
Because it bases tests on the internal structure of the software, not on the requirements specification
Because it only applies to dynamic testing techniques and not to static analysis
explanation: c) is correct. White-box testing is based on the internal structure of the software. If the software does not implement one or more requirements, white-box testing is unlikely to detect the resulting defects of omission.

stem:
Consider the following characteristics (1-4) and agile testing quadrants (A-D):

  1. Business-Facing and Critiquing the Product
  2. Technology-Facing and Critiquing the Product
  3. Business-Facing and Supporting the Team
  4. Technology-Facing and Supporting the Team
  • A. Agile testing quadrant Q1
  • B. Agile testing quadrant Q2
  • C. Agile testing quadrant Q3
  • D. Agile testing quadrant Q4

How do the following test characteristics map onto the agile testing quadrants?
explanation:
a) is correct, according to the syllabus 5.1.7. Testing Quadrants:

  • Quadrant Q1 (technology facing, support the team)

  • Quadrant Q2 (business facing, support the team)

  • Quadrant Q3 (business facing, critique the product)

  • Quadrant Q4 (technology facing, critique the product)

stem: In Exploratory Testing, which of the following statements is true regarding the role of a test charter?
options: A test charter outlines specific, detailed test cases to be executed in a predetermined order
A test charter is used to document the test results after the testing session has been completed
A test charter provides a high-level objective for a testing session, guiding the tester's exploration of the software
Test charters are not used in Exploratory Testing as they limit the tester's ability to explore the software freely
explanation: c) is correct. Exploratory testing is sometimes conducted using session-based testing to structure the testing. In a session-based approach, exploratory testing is conducted within a defined time-box. The tester uses a test charter containing test objectives to guide the testing.

stem: A Reviewer has found a major inconsistency in the work product. Their next step should be to:
options: Fix the inconsistency themselves without further discussion
Discuss the issue with the Author in a separate meeting outside the review
Raise the issue during the review meeting for discussion and resolution
Ignore the inconsistency, as it's not a Reviewer's responsibility to identify solutions
explanation: c) is correct. The reviewer's role is to identify anomalies and raise them during the review meeting (communication and analysis phase) for discussion and resolution, not to fix them directly.

stem: A tester needs to generate a large set of user profiles with realistic names, addresses, and email addresses for testing a registration system. Which tool category would best support this?
options: Management tools
Test design and implementation tools
Non-functional testing tools
Test execution and coverage tools
explanation: b) is correct. Test design and implementation tools facilitate generation of test cases, test data and test procedures.

stem: Which of the following statements about Checklist-Based Testing is FALSE?
options: Checklists can be derived from various sources, including past experience, user expectations, and an understanding of common software failures
Checklists in checklist-based testing should not contain items that are general and cover broad aspects of the software
Checklist-based testing can be applied to both functional and non-functional testing
Items on a checklist should always be specific enough to be checked automatically
explanation: d) is correct (FALSE statement). Per the syllabus 4.4.3. Checklist-Based Testing: Checklists should not contain items that can be checked automatically, items better suited as entry/exit criteria, or items that are too general.

stem:
The testing team has been testing software applications on mobile devices for a period of 5 years. New test cases are constantly added to the regression test suite, both for new functionality and for the most important and complex functionalities. Still, from time to time, users complain to the support service. According to management estimates users find in average approximately 5% of the total number of defects. The manager blames the testing team for insufficient test coverage and asks to increase the number of test cases per module.

Which of the following testing principles is most likely to help the test team explain to the manager why some defects are likely to be missed?
options: Exhaustive testing is impossible
Testing shows the presence, not the absence of defects
Absence-of-defects fallacy
All of above
explanation:
d) is correct. All three principles help explain why defects may be missed:

  • Exhaustive testing is impossible (except in trivial cases), so not everything can be tested

  • Testing shows the presence, not the absence of defects, so passing tests don't prove there are no defects

  • The absence-of-defects fallacy reminds that even defect-free software may not meet user needs

stem: In product risk analysis, how is the risk level typically calculated in a quantitative approach?
options: By creating a risk matrix and assigning scores
By estimating the cost of risk mitigation
By multiplying the risk likelihood with the risk impact
By prioritizing the risks based on stakeholder input
explanation: c) is correct. According to the syllabus: Risk assessment can use a quantitative or qualitative approach, or a mix of them. In the quantitative approach the risk level is calculated as the multiplication of risk likelihood and risk impact. In the qualitative approach the risk level can be determined using a risk matrix.

stem: Which combination of 'C' words outlines the framework used to understand and develop user stories in agile practices?
options: Condition, Communication, Closure
Context, Collaboration, Conclusion
Capture, Converse, Certify
Card, Conversation, Confirmation
explanation:
d) is correct. User stories have three critical aspects, called together the "3 C's":

  • Card – the medium describing a user story (e.g., an index card, an entry in an electronic board)

  • Conversation – explains how the software will be used (can be documented or verbal)

  • Confirmation – the acceptance criteria

stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding component testing?
options: One of the primary goals of component testing is to validate that the development environment closely matches the final production environment
Component testing, also referred to as isolation testing, aims to identify non-functional system failures and validate the functionality of individual software items that can be tested independently

Component testing may include testing of functionality (such as verifying the accuracy of calculations) and specific non-functional characteristics (such as performance testing, for instance, ensuring calculations are completed within acceptable time frames)
Component testing usually is conducted by testers rather than developers by using black-box test techniques and static analysis tools
explanation: c) is correct. Component testing may include testing of functionality (e.g., verifying accuracy of calculations) and specific non-functional characteristics (e.g., performance testing to ensure calculations are completed within acceptable time frames).

stem: During a testing period, a new defect is discovered that is causing significant delays in the testing schedule. This defect should be documented in which of the following reports?
options: Test completion report only
Test progress report only
Both test progress and test completion reports
Neither report, as defects are tracked separately
explanation: c) is correct. According to the syllabus, new defects are tracked in test progress reports, and their final status (fixed, unfixed, etc.) is included in the test completion report.

stem: A project manager is debating the inclusion of static testing techniques in the development process. They argue that testing can be done later in the development cycle. How would you explain the value of static testing in this situation?
options: Static testing is cheaper than dynamic testing later in the cycle
Static testing can detect code defects more efficiently than dynamic testing, usually resulting in a lower overall development effort
Static testing eliminates the need for dynamic testing altogether
Static testing allows for faster release cycles with fewer defects
explanation: b) is correct. Code defects can be detected using static analysis more efficiently than in dynamic testing, usually resulting in both fewer code defects and a lower overall development effort.

stem:
Customers of the TestWash car wash chain have cards with a record of the number of washes they have bought so far. The initial value is 0. After entering the car wash, the system increases the number on the card by one. This value represents the number of the current wash. Based on this number the system decides what discount the customer is entitled to.

For every third wash, the system gives a 10% discount, for every fifth wash the system gives a 20% discount, and every tenth wash is free. When the number of washes corresponds to two or more discounts, the system applies the largest possible discount.

Which of the following sets of input data (understood as the numbers of the current wash) achieves the highest equivalence partition coverage?
explanation:
c) is correct. The following valid equivalence partitions can be identified: 1. 10% discount (3, 6, 9, 12, 33, 66, 99) 2. 20% discount (5, 15, 25…) 3. Free (10, 20…100) 4. No discount (1, 2, 4, 7, 8…)

Coverage: 1 (no discount), 10 (free), 12 (10%), 25 (20%), 100 (free) — covers all 4 partitions.

stem: A software development team is preparing to release a major update to an e-commerce platform. As part of the testing process, the team is conducting a review of the requirements and specifications to identify testable features and to define test conditions. Which test activity does this process represent?
options: Test execution
Test design
Test analysis
Test planning
explanation: c) is correct. Test analysis includes analyzing the test basis to identify testable features and to define and prioritize associated test conditions, together with the related risks and risk levels. The test basis and the test objects are also evaluated to identify defects they may contain and to assess their testability. Test analysis is often supported by the use of test techniques. Test analysis answers the question "what to test?" in terms of measurable coverage criteria.

stem: A testing team needs to ensure that any modifications made to the test environment are reversible if the new changes lead to significant issues during testing. This requires a methodical approach to tracking and reverting system settings and test data. Which management practice is specifically designed to handle this requirement?
options: Change control
Data governance
Operational management
Configuration management
explanation: d) is correct. Configuration management (CM) is the discipline of identifying, controlling, and tracking changes to a system's configuration items, including software, hardware, documentation, and test data. CM enables teams to establish baselines (snapshots of the system at a specific point in time) and revert to them if changes cause problems. It also ensures that modifications are made in a controlled manner, reducing the risk of unintended consequences.

stem:
A smart home app measures the average temperature in the house over the previous week and provides feedback to the occupants on their environmental friendliness based on this temperature.

The feedback for different average temperature ranges (to the nearest °C) should be:

Using BVA (only Min- and Max values), which of the following sets of test inputs provides the highest level of boundary coverage?
explanation:
b) is correct. 5 out of 8 (10, 16, 19, 22 and 23). For the input equivalence partitions given, the above used boundary value technique yields the following 8 coverage items: 10°C, 11°C, 15°C, 16°C, 19°C, 20°C, 22°C, 23°C.

Round brackets () – values are not included, you need to take min+1, max-1. Square Brackets [] – values are included, you need to take min, max.

stem: What is the key distinction between Confirmation Testing and Regression Testing based on the given information?
options: Confirmation Testing validates new features, while Regression Testing ensures the correctness of fixed defects
Confirmation Testing is conducted after code changes, while Regression Testing occurs before code changes
Confirmation Testing confirms the successful resolution of original defects, while Regression Testing ensures that changes, including fixes, do not introduce adverse consequences
Regression Testing confirms the successful resolution of original defects, while Confirmation Testing ensures that changes, including fixes, do not introduce adverse consequences
explanation: c) is correct. Confirmation testing confirms that a failure caused by a defect does not reoccur after the fix, while regression testing ensures that changes do not introduce adverse consequences in unchanged areas.

stem: Which of the following is a direct outcome of the 'Fixing and Reporting' phase?
options: The review scope and objectives are documented
Detailed action plans are assigned to address anomalies
Participants agree on the acceptability of the work product
Defect reports are created and tracked
explanation: d) is correct. Fixing and reporting: For every defect, a defect report should be created so that corrective actions can be followed-up. Once the exit criteria are reached, the work product can be accepted. The review results are reported.

stem: Which of the following work products is NOT explicitly mentioned as part of the test implementation phase?
options: Test procedures
Test execution schedule
Test environment requirements
Test suites
explanation: c) is correct. Test implementation work products include: test procedures, automated test scripts, test suites, test data, test execution schedule, and test environment elements. Examples of test environment elements include: stubs, drivers, simulators, and service virtualizations. Test environment requirements are an output of test design.

stem:
Your team uses planning poker to estimate the test effort for a newly required feature.

Given the following user story: "I want the option to log in using my social media accounts, So I can access the platform quickly and easily without creating a separate login"

  • Each estimator has a deck of cards with values similar to the Fibonacci sequence (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21)

During the first poker planning session, the following story points were given based on risk, effort, complexity, and proper extent of testing:

  • Product owner: 5
  • Developers: 13
  • Testers: 21

Which action should the team agree on?
options: The team should choose the average value from the estimates of the product owner, developers, and testers
Another round of the planning poker session should occur, if consensus won't be reached the team should choose the average value from the estimates of the product owner, developers, and testers
Another round of the planning poker session should occur, if consensus won't be reached in the next round the user story won't be taken into the sprint backlog
Another round of the planning poker session should occur, if consensus won't be reached in the next round, another round of the planning poker session should occur
explanation: d) is correct. The poker round is repeated until an agreement is reached, either by consensus or by applying rules to limit the number of poker rounds, and the rules are not defined by the team.

stem: What is a major benefit of implementing test automation in software testing processes?
options: Test automation provides easier access to information about testing to support test management and test reporting
Test automation saves time as once automated tests are created, they never need to be updated or maintained
Test automation provides faster time to market as eliminates the need of requirements
With automation, testers no longer need to understand the system they are testing
explanation: a) is correct. Potential benefits of test automation include easier access to information about testing to support test management and test reporting (e.g., statistics, graphs, and aggregated data about test progress, defect rates, and test execution duration).

stem:
Your favorite bicycle daily rental store has just introduced a new Customer Relationship Management system and asked you, one of their most loyal members, to test it.

The implemented features are as follows:

  • Anyone can rent a bicycle, but members receive a 20% discount
  • However, if the return deadline is missed, the discount is no longer available
  • After 15 rentals, both members and non-members get a gift: a T-shirt

The decision table describing the implemented features looks as follows:

Based ONLY on the feature description of the Customer Relationship Management system, which of the above rules describes an impossible situation?
options: R3
R4
R5
R7
explanation: d) is correct. The "dash" symbol can be both T and F. F = Non-member. Non-members cannot get a discount, even if they did not miss a deadline yet.

stem: Which of the following is a typical responsibility of the test management role?
options: Analyzing test results and performance metrics to provide stakeholders with timely updates on test status, issues, and resolutions
Executing test cases according to predefined test procedures and schedules
Participating in test automation activities, including script development and maintenance
Analyzing user stories, use cases, and functional specifications to derive test scenarios and test cases
explanation: a) is correct, example of the test monitoring, control or test completion. The test management role is mainly focused on the activities of test planning, test monitoring and control, and test completion.

stem: Which of the following BEST describes a tester participating in a retrospective meeting?
options: As an automation tester, I should only attend and participate in a retrospective meeting if I have any feedback and input related to activities conducted by the team during the sprint
As a tester participating in a retrospective meeting, I should provide feedback and input on all activities conducted by the team during the sprint
As a tester, I participate in a retrospective meeting as an observer, ensuring that the meeting adheres to the retrospective rules and agile values
As a tester participating in a retrospective meeting, I should introduce topics that are related to testing only. All other subjects will be covered by different participants
explanation: b) is correct. In a retrospective, all team members discuss all activities conducted during the sprint, not just their own specialty areas.

stem:
You are testing a platform for sharing news, updates, opinions, and engaging in conversations on a wide range of topics. Users can also share multimedia content such as images and videos. The platform is accessible via the web, as well as through dedicated mobile applications. Note that the test management system used on the project has a known bug in ordering test cases. You need to execute test cases from the regression test suite in accordance with the specified execution schedule. Consider the following list of test cases, priorities and dependencies:

You also identified the following logical dependencies between test cases:

  • The user cannot write a comment if there is no post
  • If the user deletes the post, then the comment is automatically deleted

Which of the following is a possible test execution schedule that considers both priorities and dependencies?
options: TC3 - TC4 - TC5 - TC2 - TC1 - TC6
TC3 - TC4 - TC1 - TC5 - TC6 - TC2
TC3 - TC5 - TC4 - TC1 - TC2 - TC6
TC3 - TC4 - TC5 - TC1 - TC6 - TC2
explanation: d) is correct. This schedule considers both the priorities and the dependencies between test cases (posts must exist before comments, and deleting a post deletes comments).

stem:
You need to test the customer support system. The user starts in the OPEN with the user account and has the ability to log into the admin account on certain states of the ticket.

Consider the following state table for the customer support system:

Assume that each test must start at the beginning state, OPEN, and each test ends when a transition arrives at the beginning state.

Which of the following test cases, represented as sequences of events, covers ONLY valid transitions?
options: Start progress, Stop progress, Login, Start progress, Reopen
Start progress, Stop progress, Start progress, Done, Reject, Reopen
Start progress, Stop progress, Start progress, Done, Login, Reject, Reopen
Start progress, Done, Login, Reject, Start progress, Reopen
explanation: c) is correct. This sequence of events covers only valid transitions according to the state table.

stem: You've designed a complex test suite covering various edge cases and potential error conditions. Executing it requires patience and a systematic approach. This scenario primarily highlights the importance of which tester skill?
options: Domain knowledge
Testing knowledge
Creativity
Thoroughness and being methodical
explanation: d) is correct. Executing a complex test suite covering various edge cases requires patience and a systematic approach, which highlights the importance of thoroughness and being methodical.

stem:
Consider the following defect report for a mobile banking app:

Application: BankApp v2.1 Env.: Staging Defect: Unable to deposit checks via mobile app

Steps to Reproduce: 1. Log into the BankApp. 2. Navigate to the "Deposit" section. 3. Attempt to deposit a check using the mobile deposit feature.

Expected Result: The check is scanned and accepted for deposit. Actual Result: The app crashes immediately after the check is scanned.

Severity: Medium Priority: High

You received the following feedback from the quality assurance team stating that the defect described in this test report cannot be reproduced:

2023-April-10 – Jane Smith – Open After multiple attempts to reproduce the issue by scanning different checks, the application did not crash and functioned as expected. Based on the test case TC-2456, the app should seamlessly handle check deposits. This functionality is critical as outlined in REQ-0456. The problem was previously reported but now appears to be resolved.

What critical information is MISSING from this defect report that would have been useful for the developers?
options: Estimated time to fix the defect, to help prioritize the defect or set expectations for when it might be resolved
Name of the developer who's code caused the failure, to streamline the assignment of the defect to the right developer, potentially speeding up the fix
Detailed technical analysis of the root cause to save developers time by providing a starting point for debugging and potential solutions
GitHub articles about similar errors and possible resolutions, to offer potential solutions or show that the problem is known and has been addressed elsewhere
None of above
explanation:
e) is correct. None of these items are listed as essential in the syllabus. A defect report logged during dynamic testing typically includes:

  • Unique identifier

  • Title with a short summary of the anomaly being reported

  • Date when the anomaly was observed, issuing organization, and author, including their role

  • Identification of the test object and test environment

  • Context of the defect

  • Description of the failure to enable reproduction and resolution including the steps that detected the anomaly, and any relevant test logs, database dumps, screenshots, or recordings

  • Expected results and actual results

stem:
Your team analyzes the following user story to define the acceptance criteria:

As a frequent traveler, I want to be able to save my preferred airlines and airports in my profile so that the system can suggest relevant flights to me.

Which of the following test cases will NOT be relevant for this user story?
options: Input: The user accesses their profile settings and adds "Delta Airlines" to the "Preferred Airlines" list. Expected Output: The system saves the preference, and it may be visibly reflected in the user's profile.
Input: The user navigates to the flight search page. Expected Output: Flights from the user's preferred airlines (if available) are highlighted or displayed more prominently in the search results.
Input: The user clicks "Edit Profile" and removes an airport from their "Preferred Airports" list. Expected Output: The airport is removed from the saved preferences.
Input: The user selects a seat preference (window or aisle) in their profile. Expected Output: The seat preference is saved and may be used to pre-filter flight options when available.
explanation: d) is correct. While seat preferences could be a valuable feature for a travel booking site, it's unrelated to the core goal of the user story, which focuses on saving preferred airlines and airports.

stem: A key advantage of DevOps for testing is the increased focus on non-functional quality characteristics like performance and reliability. Why might DevOps be superior to traditional approaches in this area?
options: DevOps eliminates the need for performance and scalability testing on the acceptance testing level
DevOps encourages frequent deployments, allowing for earlier detection of non-functional issues
DevOps prioritizes manual testing, which is better suited for non-functional testing
DevOps reduces communication between development and testing teams by automatically creating non-functional defect reports
explanation:
b) is correct. From the testing perspective, some of the benefits of DevOps are:

  • Fast feedback on the code quality, and whether changes adversely affect existing code

  • CI promotes a shift-left approach in testing by encouraging developers to submit high quality code accompanied by component tests and static analysis

  • Promotes automated processes like CI/CD that facilitate establishing stable test environments

  • Increases the view on non-functional quality characteristics (e.g., performance, reliability)

  • Automation through a delivery pipeline reduces the need for repetitive manual testing

stem: What is the primary focus of quality assurance (QA)?
options: Correcting defects in the product
Achieving appropriate levels of quality in the product
Implementing and improving processes
Conducting formal methods such as model checking
explanation: c) is correct. QA is a process-oriented, preventive approach that focuses on the implementation and improvement of processes. It works on the basis that if a good process is followed correctly, then it will generate a good product. QA applies to both the development and testing processes, and is the responsibility of everyone on a project.

stem: Which of the following is a good testing practice that applies to all software development lifecycles?
options: During the SDLC, test analysis and design for a specific test level begin alongside its corresponding development phase
Test analysis and design are carried out during the early stages of the SDLC, while test implementation and execution occur during later phases
During the initial stages of SDLC, testing responsibilities lie with developers, while testers assume testing duties in later stages
Test closure activities serve as the final sign-off to determine the approval status of deployment
explanation: a) is correct. Test analysis and design for a given test level should start during the corresponding development phase to facilitate early testing (e.g., acceptance test analysis and design should begin during requirements analysis).

stem: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of early feedback?
options: Avoiding requirements misunderstandings, which may not have been detected until later in the development cycle when they are more expensive to fix
Clarifying customer feature requests, making them available for customer use early. This way, the product better reflects what the customer wants
Early and frequent feedback reduces the need for comprehensive requirements
Discovering (via continuous integration), isolating, and resolving quality problems early
explanation: c) is correct. Early and frequent feedback does not reduce the need for comprehensive requirements. The benefits of early feedback include: avoiding requirements misunderstandings; clarifying customer feature requests; and discovering, isolating, and resolving quality problems early.

stem: A tester is tasked with ensuring that every possible decision outcome within a complex algorithm has been executed by test cases. Which technique is BEST aligned with this goal?
options: State transition testing
Branch testing
Error guessing
Decision table testing
explanation: b) is correct. Branch coverage specifically targets ensuring that every possible path (outcome) of a decision point (e.g., if/else statements, loops) within the code has been tested. This directly aligns with the goal of covering all decision outcomes in the algorithm.

stem: Which of the following is true regarding the test pyramid?
options: The pyramid layers represent the granularity levels of tests, with higher layers indicating higher test granularity
The pyramid layers represent the granularity levels of tests, with lower layers indicating lower test granularity
The pyramid layers represent groups of tests, and higher layers correspond to lower test granularity
The pyramid layers represent the granularity levels of tests, and the test granularity is nearly the same across all pyramid layers
explanation: c) is correct. In the test pyramid, the layers represent groups of tests, and the higher the layer, the lower the test granularity (i.e., tests become broader and less granular as you move up the pyramid).

stem: What role do customers or product owners play in the Whole Team Approach to testing in agile methodologies?
options: They are responsible for creating test cases and testing the software
They provide clarification on requirements and participate in acceptance testing
They solely focus on funding and marketing the software product
They are excluded from the testing process to maintain objectivity in quality assessment
explanation: b) is correct. Testers work closely with other team members to ensure that the desired quality levels are achieved. This includes collaborating with business representatives to help them create suitable acceptance tests.

stem: You have tested 10 out of 40 branches on a module of code. Which of the following situations could explain this?
options: 5% of conditional branches have been tested with only one outcome (true or false)
10% of unconditional branches have been tested
25% branch coverage is achieved
10% of all statements in the code have been executed
explanation: c) is correct. Branch coverage = (number of tested branches / total number of branches) × 100% = 10/40 × 100% = 25%.

stem: Which of the following BEST defines EXIT criteria in a testing project?
options: The ratio of failed-to-pass test cases is less than one to one hundred
All test cases and test suites are prioritized based on coverage-based prioritization
Databases with dummy data are configured and linked to the proper environments
The specification for third-party integration has been updated with relevant information for a new version
explanation: a) is correct. Exit criteria define when testing is complete and typically include measures like the ratio of failed-to-pass test cases. The other options describe entry criteria or other test activities, not exit criteria.

stem: Which one of the following answers describes the Behavior-Driven Development (BDD)?
options: A software development technique in which the test cases are developed, automated and then the software is developed incrementally to pass those test cases
A collaboration-based test-first approach that defines acceptance tests in the stakeholders' domain language
A collaborative approach to development in which the team is focusing on delivering expected behavior of a component or system for the customer, which forms the basis for testing
collaborative approach to development where tests are structured into scenarios which represent use cases of the software under test. The scripts can be parameterized with test data.
explanation:
c) is correct. BDD is a collaborative approach to development in which the team focuses on delivering the expected behavior of a component or system for the customer, which forms the basis for testing.

Note: b) describes Acceptance Test-Driven Development (ATDD), a) describes Test-Driven Development (TDD), and d) describes keyword-driven testing.

stem: How does white-box testing contribute to the overall quality of software testing when combined with black-box testing?
options: By ensuring that the testing process is solely based on the high quality requirements specification
By providing an objective measure of code coverage, which complements the functional testing of black-box techniques
By completely replacing the need for black-box testing, thus making the process more efficient
By focusing exclusively on the requirements ans use cases, thereby covering all aspects of system testing
explanation: b) is correct. White-box testing provides an objective measure of code coverage, which complements the functional testing performed by black-box techniques. Together they provide better overall test coverage and quality.

stem: Which of the following could be a defect in the online shop?
options: An invalid number of products is added to the cart when the user clicks the "Add" button
The "Proceed to checkout" button becomes disabled when the user clicks the "Remove" button, but there is another type of product in the cart
The multiplication function is written in the code instead of the addition function
After clicking the "Clear cart" button, the products remain in the cart
explanation: c) is correct. According to the syllabus 1.2.3. Errors, Defects, Failures, and Root Causes and the glossary: Defect - An imperfection or deficiency in a work product where it does not meet its requirements or specifications. Defects can be found in a test script, in source code, or in a supporting artifact such as a build file. The other options describe failures (observable incorrect behavior), not defects.

stem: In the context of product risk control, what does risk mitigation involve?
options: Accepting the risk and its potential consequences
Transferring the risk to another party or entity
Implementing actions to reduce the probability or impact of the risk
Creating a contingency plan to address the risk if it occurs
explanation: c) is correct. This is the correct definition of risk mitigation. It involves proactive measures to decrease the likelihood of a risk occurring or lessen its impact on the project or product.

stem: You are developing a checklist for a new project and notice that many items are similar to a checklist from a previous project. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Use the existing checklist without change, as it saves time and effort
Discard the old checklist entirely and create a fresh one from scratch
Adapt the existing checklist, reviewing its effectiveness and incorporating insights from defect data analysis
Copy the old checklist and add only new, untested items for additional coverage
explanation: c) is correct. Checklists need to evolve to stay relevant. Adapting an existing checklist while considering past defects is the most balanced approach. The other options are extreme: reusing without change risks missing new issues, starting from scratch is wasteful, and adding untested items can bloat the checklist.

stem: Which of these statements is NOT a factor that contributes to successful reviews?
options: Providing detailed and constructive feedback to authors and stakeholders
Conducting reviews only on equal, proportional chunks, so that it is easier to count the required number of the reviews
Defining clear objectives and measurable exit criteria for the review process
Choosing the appropriate review type to achieve the given objectives
explanation: b) is correct. Factors contributing to successful reviews include: providing detailed and constructive feedback, defining clear objectives and measurable exit criteria, and choosing the appropriate review type. Reviewing documents in small chunks (ideally small enough so that reviewers can review them in less than an hour) helps, but requiring "equal, proportional chunks" for counting purposes is not a success factor.

stem: When considering the implementation of test automation, which of the following factors poses the LEAST significant risk?
options: Unrealistic expectations about the immediate benefits of automation
Potential vendor issues if support or updates are discontinued
The cost and ongoing effort required for test script maintenance
Automation tools introducing their own complex bugs into the system
explanation: d) is correct. Automation tools do not typically introduce bugs into the system under test, as they operate on the system rather than modifying it. The significant risks of test automation include: unrealistic expectations, underestimating the cost/effort of maintaining testware, and excessive reliance on tool vendors.

stem: Identify the statement that is LEAST likely to be true about the error guessing technique
options: It can help uncover defects that might be missed by structured test design techniques
It is guaranteed to find all critical defects within the software
Its effectiveness can vary depending on the tester's skills and experience
It can supplement other testing approaches to enhance overall test coverage
explanation: b) is correct. Error guessing is an experience-based technique that is not guaranteed to find all critical defects. Its effectiveness depends on the tester's skills and experience, and it is best used to supplement other testing approaches.

stem: Mr. Test has been testing software applications on mobile devices for a period of 5 years. He has a wealth of experience in testing mobile applications and achieves better results in a shorter time than others. Over several months, Mr. Test did not modify the existing automated test cases and did not create any new test cases. This leads to fewer and fewer defects being found by executing the tests. What principle of testing did Mr. Test not observe?
options: Testing depends on the environment
Exhaustive testing is not possible
Repeating of same tests will not find new defects
Defects cluster together
explanation: c) is correct. Principle #5 says "If the same tests are repeated over and over again, eventually these tests no longer find any new defects. To detect new defects, existing tests and test data may need changing, and new tests may need to be written." Automated regression testing of the same test cases will not bring new findings.

stem:
Consider the following test categories (1-4) and agile testing quadrants (A-D):

  1. Usability testing
  2. API testing
  3. Performance testing
  4. Unit integration testing

A. Agile testing quadrant Q1: technology facing, supporting the development team B. Agile testing quadrant Q2: business facing, supporting the development team C. Agile testing quadrant Q3: business facing, critique the product D. Agile testing quadrant Q4: technology facing, critique the product

How do the following test categories map onto the agile testing quadrants?
explanation:
d) is correct, according to the syllabus 5.1.7. Testing Quadrants:

  • Quadrant Q1 contains component and component integration tests

  • Quadrant Q2 contains functional tests, examples, user story tests, user experience prototypes, API testing, and simulations

  • Quadrant Q3 contains exploratory testing, usability testing, user acceptance testing

  • Quadrant Q4 contains smoke tests and non-functional tests (except usability tests)

stem:
Consider this acceptance criterion for a user story on an e-learning platform:

  • Given the user has completed a module
  • When the user clicks "Mark as Complete"
  • Then the module's status should change to "Completed"
  • And the user's overall progress should be updated

Which format best describes this acceptance criterion?
options: Rule-oriented
Process-oriented
Decision table
Scenario-oriented
explanation: d) is correct. The rule-oriented format includes formats like bullet point verification lists or tabulated forms of input-output mappings, explicitly showing the rules to be followed. Given/When/Then is a scenario-oriented format because it describes a scenario to be verified.

stem:
Your project involves building a language learning app catering to the needs of an online tutoring service.

Your task is:

"To check the degree to which a component or system uses time, resources and capacity when accomplishing its designated functions"

What type of testing are you MOST LIKELY performing?
options: Functional testing
Non-functional testing
Load testing
Stress testing
explanation: b) is correct. Performance efficiency (the degree to which a component or system uses time, resources and capacity when accomplishing its designated functions) is tested in the scope of non-functional testing.

stem: Which of the following is the LEAST important aspect of communicating test status to business stakeholders?
options: Detailed transcripts of daily stand-up meetings
The overall percentage of test cases passed vs. failed
The potential impact of identified defects on end-users
The estimated timeline for resolving critical defects
explanation: a) is correct. These meetings are primarily for the development and testing teams to synchronize their work. Business stakeholders are typically not involved in these daily updates and would find the detailed transcripts irrelevant to their needs.

stem: Which activity is an example of static testing in the context of software development?
options: Executing the software under test conditions to identify any defects
Running automated scripts to test the software's interface
Using a tool to analyze the source code for complex code patterns that could lead to errors
Monitoring the software's performance in a production environment
explanation: c) is correct. Code, process specification, system architecture specification or other work products are evaluated through manual examination (e.g., reviews) or with the help of a tool (e.g., static analysis). Static analysis can identify problems prior to dynamic testing while often requiring less effort, since no test cases are required, and tools are typically used. Static analysis is often incorporated into CI frameworks. While largely used to detect specific code defects, static analysis is also used to evaluate maintainability and security.

stem:
You are testing a card number validator for a Visa card type, which accepts valid card numbers and rejects invalid card numbers. A card number is a sequence of digits. A card number is valid if it consists of sixteen digits. If the number of digits is less than 16, the system displays an error, "Card number is too short.". If the number of digits is more than 16, the system displays an error, "Card number is too long.". A Visa card number is valid if it starts with 4. You have identified the following valid equivalence partitions:

Variable: Card number first digit

  • The partition "first digit is correct" - Card number starts with 4
  • The partition "first digit is incorrect" - Card number doesn't start with 4

Variable: Card number length

  • The partition "length correct" - sixteen-digit card number
  • The partition "length is too short" - Card numbers with length less than 16
  • The partition "length is too long" - Card numbers with length more than 16

Which of the following is a MINIMUM set of input test data that covers all identified equivalence partitions?
explanation: d) is correct. 5 out of 5. Each invalid value covers only one of the invalid partitions avoiding 'failures masking'. When invalid equivalence partitions are used in test cases, they should be tested individually, i.e., not combined with other invalid equivalence partitions, to ensure that failures are not masked. Failures can be masked when several failures occur at the same time but only one is visible, causing the other failures to be undetected.

stem: How does the business domain context factor influence testing?
options: It dictates the specific test automation tools to be used
It mainly affects the timing and duration of the testing phase
It influences the criticality of the test object, identified risks, and compliance with specific legal regulations
It is only relevant for deciding the test team's size
explanation: c) is correct. The way the testing is carried out will depend on a number of contextual factors including: Business domain (criticality of the test object, identified risks, market needs, specific legal regulations, etc.)

stem: Which of the following is NOT a responsibility of Configuration Management?
options: Identifying and controlling test plans, strategies, and scripts
Tracking changes and versions of test environments and other test items
Deciding the priority of defects found during testing
Maintaining records of changed configuration items when a new baseline is created
explanation: c) is correct. This is NOT a responsibility of CM. While CM helps track defects, the prioritization is typically handled by the testing team or project management based on the severity and impact of the defects.

stem:
A speed control and reporting system has the following characteristics:

The speed in km/h is available to the system as an integer value.

Which would be the most likely set of values (km/h) identified by applying the 2-value boundary value analysis (BVA), where only the values on the boundaries of the equivalence classes are selected?
explanation:
c) is correct. Includes all necessary boundary values. The following partitions can be identified: 1. <= 50, boundary value 50 2. 51 – 55, boundary values 51, 55 3. 56 – 60, boundary values 56, 60 4. >= 61, boundary value 61

Boundary value according to glossary V.3.2: A minimum or maximum value of an ordered equivalence partition.

stem:
You work as a tester on a language learning app for an international education platform.

Your task is:

"To test changes to a production system, encompassing the assessment of implementation success and the detection of potential regressions in unaffected areas, typically comprising the majority of the system"

What testing are you MOST LIKELY performing?
options: Regression testing
Confirmation testing
Maintenance testing
Acceptance testing
explanation: c) is correct. Testing the changes to a system in production includes both evaluating the success of the implementation of the change and the checking for possible regressions in parts of the system that remain unchanged (which is usually most of the system).

stem: Which review type relies heavily on the expertise of a moderator to guide the process and ensure consensus and decision-making regarding technical problems?
options: Informal Review
Walkthrough
Technical Review
Inspection
explanation: c) is correct. A technical review is performed by technically qualified reviewers and led by a moderator. The objectives of a technical review are to gain consensus and make decisions regarding a technical problem, but also to detect anomalies, evaluate quality and build confidence in the work product, generate new ideas, and to motivate and enable authors to improve.

stem: The task of evaluating the testability of the requirements and system is a key component of which testing activity?
options: Test analysis
Test planning
Test design
Test execution
explanation: a) is correct. Test analysis includes analyzing the test basis to identify testable features and to define and prioritize associated test conditions, together with the related risks and risk levels. The test basis and the test objects are also evaluated to identify defects they may contain and to assess their testability. Test analysis is often supported by the use of test techniques. Test analysis answers the question "what to test?" in terms of measurable coverage criteria.

stem:
Your team uses planning poker to estimate the test effort for a newly required feature.

Given the following user story: "As an online shopper, I want to easily clear items from my shopping cart, So I can quickly remove unwanted products and proceed to checkout with my desired items"

Each estimator has a deck of cards with values similar to the Fibonacci sequence (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21)

Previously, the planning poker sessions were frequently delayed and prolonged, averaging four rounds each. During a retrospective meeting, the team collectively decided to implement new planning poker rules:

  • R1: If someone that a user story is big, they assign an estimate of 100;
  • R2: The planning poker sessions are constrained to a maximum of two sessions per user story
  • R3: If no consensus is reached in the second round, then the final estimated value is the average between the most optimistic estimation and the most pessimistic estimation
  • R4: If two or more team members estimate 100 points in the second round, then the user story should be broken down into multiple smaller stories
  • R5: If only one member of the team in the second round puts an estimate of 100 points, then the third session of planning poker is required

After two rounds, the consensus was not reached, so the third round was initiated. You can see the test estimation results in the table below.

What value should IDEALLY be accepted by the team, and why?
options: Accept 13 as the consensus is reached in the third round
Accept 8 as the final estimate as this has most of the votes in the second round
Accept 13 as the average value between the most optimistic and pessimistic estimations
Accept 10 as the average value between estimates of all team members
explanation: c) is correct. The team has decided on the R3, "If no consensus is reached in the second round, then the final estimated value is the average between the most optimistic estimation and the most pessimistic estimation". This is what the team should do ideally. (Note: a) is not correct because the team broke the R2 rule by holding a third session.)

stem: To improve the quality of code, a tester decides to systematically review the source code for potential flaws before it goes into the execution phase. Which type of tool is most appropriate for this activity?
options: Static testing tools
Non-functional testing tools
Test design and implementation tools
Test execution and coverage tools
explanation: a) is correct. Static testing tools (e.g., static analysis tools) are used to systematically review source code for potential flaws before execution, without running the code.

stem:
Your favorite bicycle daily rental store has just introduced a new Customer Relationship Management system and asked you, one of their most loyal members, to test it.

The implemented features are as follows:

  • Anyone can rent a bicycle, but members receive a 20% discount
  • However, if the return deadline is missed, the discount is no longer available
  • After 10 rentals, members get a gift: a T-Shirt
  • After 10 rentals, not a member gets a gift: One free rental

The decision table describing the implemented features looks as follows:

So far you have designed the following test cases:

  • TC1: The member who missed the return deadline on the first rental
  • TC2: The member who returned the bike on time on the tenth rental
  • TC3: Not a member who returned the bike on time on the tenth rental
  • TC4: Not a member who missed the return deadline on the first rental

Which of the following test cases, when added to the existing set of test cases, will increase the decision table coverage?
options: The member who missed the return deadline on the second rental
The member who missed the return deadline on the tenth rental
Not a member who missed the return deadline on the tenth rental
Not a member who returned the bike on time on the first rental
explanation: b) is correct. The existing test cases cover rules R2 (TC1), R3 (TC2), R6 (TC3), and R5 (TC4). Only R4 (member, missed deadline, 10th rental → T-Shirt but no discount) is not covered. Option b) covers R4, increasing decision table coverage. The other options map to already-covered rules.

stem: Which statement below is incorrect when considering the benefits of traceability between the test basis and test work products?
options: Traceability between the test basis and testware allows identifying which test cases are affected by changes in the requirements
Traceability between the test basis and testware may make understanding the impact of changes more challenging
Traceability between the test basis and testware may be mandatory according to IT governance criteria
Traceability between the test basis and testware evaluates the completeness of test execution, making testing auditable
explanation: b) is correct (the incorrect statement). Good traceability makes understanding the impact of changes EASIER, not more challenging.
