The benefits of traceability include: identifying which test cases are affected by changes in the requirements, evaluating the completeness of test execution (making testing auditable), and meeting IT governance criteria where mandatory.

stem: Which of the following statements about retrospectives is true?
options: Team members can highlight problems with requirements and acceptance criteria and suggest improvements and fixes to these issues
Retrospectives are meetings generally held at the start and at the end of each iteration
The meeting focuses on how to identify responsible parties for any failures in the previous release and how to incorporate the identified improvements into their work
A retrospective meeting can harm team unity, as it can clearly show who performed well in the previous iteration and who did not
explanation: a) is correct. In retrospectives, team members can highlight problems with requirements and acceptance criteria and suggest improvements and fixes to these issues. Retrospectives are held at the end of each iteration (not the start), focus on process improvement (not blaming individuals), and are meant to build team unity.

stem:
You are testing a mobile application that serves as a comprehensive platform for managing email on smartphones and tablets. This app allows users to seamlessly access, organize, and respond to emails directly from their mobile devices. You need to execute test cases from the regression test suite in accordance with the specified execution schedule. Consider the following list of test cases, priorities and coverages:

Your objective is to prioritize test cases through additional coverage prioritization, wherein the test case achieving the highest coverage is executed first, and each subsequent test case is prioritized based on achieving the highest additional coverage. In case the coverage percentage achieved by test cases is the same, the test case with the highest priority is executed first.

Which test case should be executed as the LAST one?
options: TC2
TC3
TC4
TC5
explanation:
c) is correct. Execution order by additional coverage prioritization:

  • TC1 - Req2, Req3, Req5 (3/7, 43%) (P:High); TC2 - Req1, Req6 (2/7, 29%) (P:High); TC3 - Req2, Req4, Req5 (3/7, 43%) (P:Medium); TC4 - Req1, Req3, Req4 (3/7, 43%) (P:Low); TC5 - Req7 (1/7, 14%) (P:Low) → TC1 executed first (highest coverage, highest priority among ties)

  • Updated coverage: TC2 - Req1, Req6 (2/7, 29%); TC3 - Req4 (1/7); TC4 - Req1, Req4 (2/7); TC5 - Req7 (1/7) → TC2 executed second

  • Updated coverage: TC3 - Req4 (1/7); TC4 - Req4 (1/7); TC5 - Req7 (1/7) → TC3 executed third (Medium priority wins tie)

  • Updated coverage: TC4 - Req4 (0/7, 0%); TC5 - Req7 (1/7) → TC5 executed fourth

  • TC4 executed LAST (adds no additional coverage)

stem:
Consider the following state transition diagram for the e-banking system.

In a future release, a new feature will be introduced: the cache system. The diagram and test cases primarily focus on the new cache functionality. The cache operates as follows: when the user moves from one state to another, the previous state will be cached. Thus, each time a timeout occurs, the user should enter the PIN. Once a valid PIN is entered, the user is returned to the state they were in before the timeout.

Which of the following test cases, represented as sequences of events, achieves the highest level of valid transitions coverage?
options: valid credit card → valid pin → withdraw → timeout → valid pin → withdraw → valid amount
valid credit card → valid pin → timeout → valid pin → invalid amount → valid amount
valid credit card → valid pin → timeout → valid pin → withdraw → valid amount
valid credit card → valid pin → timeout → valid pin → invalid amount → timeout → invalid pin
explanation:
c) is correct. Valid transitions coverage = 6/10 = 60%. Before the "timeout" event the user is in the S3 ("Your balance") state, which will be cached. The "timeout" event has the action cache=S3. Which means that valid event should be "valid pin [cache = S3] / cache = S2" which returns user back to the "Your balance" state but with second "valid pin" transition.

Note: a) is incorrect (5/10 = 40%) because after timeout from S4 ("Withdraw & transfer"), the valid pin returns the user to S4 directly (via cache), so the second "withdraw" event is not a valid transition.

stem: What is meant by the term "independence of testing" in software development?
options: It refers to the testing team's autonomy to decide when to start testing
It indicates the ability of testing to operate without any external dependencies
It signifies the separation of testing activities from development to avoid bias
It denotes the testing team's independence from project management directives
explanation: c) is correct. A certain degree of independence makes the tester more effective at finding defects due to differences between the author's and the tester's cognitive biases.

stem:
You are conducting tests on the date filtering functionality of a project management tool, designed to enable users to search for projects by entering specific dates in the format YYYY-MM-DD. The test aims to verify that the system correctly displays projects corresponding to the input dates. Below are the details from the testing session:

  • Module: Project Search Module v3.12
  • Test Case Set: PCS-1
  • Number of Test Cases: 4
  • Test Run ID: 2950

  • Start Time: 09:22:00.456

  • 09:22:00.456 Execution of TC1. Input: "2023-12-01" → Output: 3 projects → Result: Passed

  • 09:22:00.457 Execution of TC2. Input: "2023-01-12" → Output: 2 projects → Result: Passed
  • 09:22:00.458 Execution of TC3. Input: "2023-12-30" → Output: error message "Invalid date" → Result: Failed
  • 09:22:00.459 Execution of TC4. Input: "2023-30-12" → Output: 2 projects → Result: Passed
  • Total time of test cycle: 0:00:00.006

Given these test results, which of the following provides the BEST description of the failure that can be used in a defect report?
options: The system erroneously rejects valid date formats while incorrectly accepting non-standard date formats. Reference: TC3, TC4
The system inconsistently adheres to the specified date format YYYY-MM-DD, resulting in both false rejections and incorrect acceptances. Reference: TC3, TC4
The date validation logic is flawed, leading to the acceptance of improperly formatted dates and the rejection of valid ones. Reference: TC3, TC4
There is a significant inconsistency in date format handling, as the system fails to standardize date input validation. Reference: TC3, TC4
explanation: b) is correct. This answer clearly points out the inconsistency in how the system handles the date format specification, making it easy to understand that there is a fundamental problem in validating both correctly and incorrectly formatted dates.

stem:
Consider the following user story:

  • As a Project Manager,
  • I want to track project progress on a dashboard,
  • so that I can ensure the project stays on schedule.

Acceptance Criteria:

  • The user can log in to the project management system with a "Project Manager" role
  • The project manager can view current project statuses
  • The project manager can update project milestones
  • The project manager can add comments to each project
  • The project manager can archive completed projects

Which of the following is the BEST example of an ATDD test for this user story?
options: Test if the project manager can update the status of ongoing projects. Expected result: The project status is updated successfully on the dashboard.
Test if a team member can log in and view project statuses. Expected result: The team member can see all current project statuses
Test if the project manager can generate financial reports for projects. Expected result: The system produces a detailed financial report
Test if the project manager can delegate tasks to team members directly from the dashboard. Expected result: Tasks are assigned to team members.
explanation: a) is correct. This test covers two acceptance criteria: updating project milestones (a form of status) and viewing the updates directly on the dashboard, ensuring the changes are visible and effective.

stem: Which statement regarding the shift-left approach is correct?
options: Code, process specifications, system architecture specifications, or other work products are evaluated through manual examination (reviews) or with the assistance of a tool (static analysis)
The shift-left approach involves the use of static analysis and achieving high coverage of unit tests, providing a viable alternative to manual exploratory testing
In the shift-left approach, non-functional test types tend to be conducted later in the SDLC when a complete system and a representative test environment are available
Testers don't require extra training as the test cases are automatically translated into executable tests
explanation:
a) is correct. The shift-left approach emphasizes early testing through static testing techniques: code, process specifications, system architecture specifications, or other work products are evaluated through manual examination (reviews) or with the assistance of a tool (static analysis). This enables early defect detection when defects are cheaper to fix.

End of Sample Exam VIII - Quiz 14 (40 questions)

stem: Which of the following statements is a valid objective for testing?
options: Building confidence in the quality level of the test object by reducing the risk level
To start testing immediately after the developers deploy the feature to the test environment
Reducing the level of risk of inadequate software quality by blocking the release till all high severity issues are not fixed
Write a test plan with high-level test cases for more accurate estimates
explanation: a) is correct. Typical test objectives include: building confidence in the quality of the test object and reducing the level of risk of inadequate software quality.

stem: Which of the options does not accurately reflect how the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) methodology influences the testing?
options: It determines the specific testing techniques to be used during the testing phase
It influences the sequence of testing activities throughout the project
It directly determines the testing budget allocated to a project
It influences the selection of testing tools and automation frameworks
explanation:
c) is correct. Testing must be adapted to the SDLC to succeed. The choice of the SDLC impacts on the:

  • Scope and timing of test activities (e.g., test levels and test types)

  • Choice of test techniques and test approach

  • Extent of test automation

The SDLC does not directly determine the testing budget.

stem: In the context of static testing, which of the following would be the most challenging to test?
options: A stylesheet (CSS) for a landing page and HTML templates for the user interface of an in-house developed CRM system
Sequence diagram for system workflows and use case specification for a software feature
Test logs and defect reports
Third-party commercial video game engines with no public codebase
explanation: d) is correct. Work products that are not appropriate for static testing include those that are difficult to interpret by human beings and that should not be analyzed by tools (e.g., 3rd party executable code due to legal reasons).

stem: Which of the following best describes the basis for creating test cases in white-box testing?
options: The internal structure and processing of the test object
The functional specifications and requirements of the software
The tester's experience and knowledge of common defects
The anticipated use of the software by end-users
explanation: a) is correct. White-box testing derives test cases from the internal structure and processing of the test object (e.g., code, statements, branches).

stem:
Consider the following definitions and match the keyword (1-4) with the definition (A-D)

  1. Risk analysis
  2. Risk control
  3. Risk likelihood
  4. Risk impact

A. The overall process of risk identification and risk assessment B. The probability that a risk will become an actual outcome or event C. The damage that will be caused if the risk becomes an actual outcome or event D. The overall process of risk mitigation and risk monitoring
explanation:
c) is correct.

  • Risk analysis (1) = A: The overall process of risk identification and risk assessment

  • Risk control (2) = D: The overall process of risk mitigation and risk monitoring

  • Risk likelihood (3) = B: The probability that a risk will become an actual outcome or event

  • Risk impact (4) = C: The damage that will be caused if the risk becomes an actual outcome or event

stem: The Whole Team Approach emphasizes collaboration and shared responsibility. Which of the following scenarios best reflects this principle?
options: Developers write all the code, testers identify bugs during testing, and business analysts document the final product
Testers work with developers to define the test strategy and collaborate with business representatives on acceptance criteria
The project manager assigns separate tasks to each team and holds them accountable for individual deliverables
Testers write automated scripts to minimize human interaction during the testing process so business representatives can use it
explanation: b) is correct. Testers work closely with other team members to ensure that the desired quality levels are achieved. This includes collaborating with business representatives to help them create suitable acceptance tests and working with developers to agree on the test strategy and decide on test automation approaches. Testers can thus transfer testing knowledge to other team members and influence the development of the product.

stem: Your test suite consists of three tests: Test A, Test B, and Test C, achieving 65%, 30%, and 55% statement coverage respectively on the same codebase. Which of the following must be true?
options: The combined test suite achieves 160% statement coverage
There exists at least one statement that must have been executed by both A and B
There exists at least one statement that must have been executed by both B and C
There exists at least one statement that must have been executed by both A and C
explanation: d) is correct. If the statements executed by A and C were disjoint, their combined coverage would be 65% + 55% = 120%, which is impossible. Coverage is always defined as the percentage of the covered elements and cannot exceed 100%. Therefore, at least 20% of executable statements must have been executed by both A and C. (A+B = 95% and B+C = 85% are both under 100%, so overlap is not guaranteed for those pairs.)

stem:
Can the following information be found in the test plan?

Test Completion Report

...

  1. Summary The testing phase for the [Project Name] has been successfully completed. This report provides an overview of the testing activities, outcomes, and recommendations for future improvements.

  2. Objectives The primary objectives of the testing phase were to:

  • Validate the functionality of [specific modules/features].
  • Identify and report defects or issues.
  • Ensure compatibility across various environments.

...

  1. Test Results
  • Test Cases Executed: [Number of test cases executed]
  • Pass: [Number of test cases passed]
  • Fail: [Number of test cases failed]
  • Blocked: [Number of test cases blocked]
  1. Defect Summary
  • Total Defects Identified: [Total number of defects]
  • Critical: [Number of critical defects]
  • Major: [Number of major defects]
  • Minor: [Number of minor defects]
  1. Recommendations
  • Provide any recommendations for improvement based on the testing experience.
  • Suggestions for future testing processes or tools that could enhance efficiency.
options: Yes, the test completion report template can be found in the communication section
Yes, the test progress report can be found in the communication section
Yes, the completion report template can be found in the stakeholders section
No, the test completion report can't be found in the test plan
explanation: a) is correct. According to the syllabus 5.1.1, the test plan may include documentation templates such as the test completion report template in the communications section.

stem:
What are the primary goals of Acceptance Test-Driven Development (ATDD)?

  • i. Verify that acceptance criteria are met
  • ii. Find higher-level defects early in user story development
  • iii. Achieve 100% statement and branch coverage
  • iv. Improve collaboration between all stakeholders and the team
  • v. Expresses the desired behavior of an application with test cases written in a simple form of natural language
options: i, iii, iv
ii, iv
i, ii, iv
i, ii, iv, v
explanation: c) is correct. The primary goals of ATDD are: verifying that acceptance criteria are met, finding higher-level defects early in user story development, and improving collaboration between all stakeholders and the team. (Note: v describes BDD, not ATDD; iii is not an ATDD goal.)

stem: You find a potential defect during white box testing. Which of the following pieces of information would be MOST valuable when reporting the defect?
options: Detailed steps on how to reproduce the issue from a user perspective
The specific line of code where the error likely occurs
A suggestion for another testing technique to confirm the bug
An assessment of the defect priority based on the user requirements
explanation: b) is correct. Because white box testing focuses on the internal structure and implementation of the software, identifying the exact line of code, function, or component where the defect resides provides the direct and most valuable technical feedback for the developer to quickly resolve the issue.

stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the difference between testing and debugging?
options: Testing identifies the source of defects; debugging analyzes the defects and proposes prevention activities
Dynamic testing shows failures caused by defects; debugging eliminates the defects, which are the source of failures
Testing removes faults; but debugging removes defects that cause the faults
Dynamic testing prevents the causes of errors; debugging removes the failures
explanation: b) is correct. Dynamic testing can show failures that are caused by defects in the software. Debugging eliminates the defects, which are the source of failures.

stem: Which Agile testing quadrant's tests are user-oriented and often manual?
options: Quadrant Q1
Quadrant Q2
Quadrant Q3
Quadrant Q4
explanation: c) is correct, according to the syllabus 5.1.7. Testing Quadrants. Quadrant Q1 tests should be automated and included in the CI process; Quadrant Q2 tests check the acceptance criteria and can be manual or automated; Quadrant Q3 tests are user-oriented and often manual; Quadrant Q4 tests are often automated.

stem:
Consider this list a tester uses when designing test cases:

  • A registration form rejects valid email addresses due to an overly restrictive validation pattern
  • A report should display dates as MM/DD/YYYY but shows them as YYYY-MM-DD
  • A discount system meant for customers with over 5 purchases doesn't trigger the discount if they have exactly 5 purchases
  • Module A sends a timestamp with milliseconds, but module B expects seconds, leading to time discrepancies

Which testing technique are these test conditions MOST LIKELY associated with?
options: Exploratory testing
Checklist-based testing
Fault attack
Boundary value analysis
explanation: c) is correct. This is a list of possible failures. Fault attacks are a methodical approach to the implementation of error guessing and require the tester to create or acquire a list of possible errors, defects and failures, and to design tests that will identify defects associated with the errors, expose the defects, or cause the failures.

stem: Which of the following roles is typically responsible for deciding what work products will be reviewed and allocating necessary resources?
options: Review Leader
Author
Scribe
Manager
explanation: d) is correct. Manager – decides what is to be reviewed and provides resources, such as staff and time for the review.

stem: Which category of testing tools is best suited for testing the performance and security aspects of an application, which are often challenging to assess manually?
options: Static testing tools
Test design and implementation tools
Non-functional testing tools
Management tools
explanation: c) is correct. Non-functional testing tools – allow the tester to perform non-functional testing that is difficult or impossible to perform manually.

stem: You're urgently asked to assess a newly developed web-based game before an unexpected early release. The requirements are mostly visual design concepts, but you have a background in gaming and are familiar with common playability pitfalls. Which testing technique aligns BEST with this situation?
options: Checklist-Based Testing
Black-box testing
Exploratory Testing
Error Guessing
explanation: c) is correct. Exploratory testing is useful when there are few or inadequate specifications or there is significant time pressure on the testing. Exploratory testing will be more effective if the tester is experienced, has domain knowledge and has a high degree of essential skills, like analytical skills, curiosity and creativeness.

stem: A software development team is debating when to start testing their project. Some team members argue for postponing testing until all features are implemented, while others advocate for starting testing early. According to testing principles, what would be the most appropriate course of action in this scenario, and why?
options: Start testing early to save time for automation testing in future
Start testing early to identify defects sooner and reduce the risk of late-stage issues
Begin testing after all features are implemented to minimize rework
Delay testing until after user acceptance testing to align with stakeholder expectations
explanation: b) is correct. Testing principle #3: Early testing saves time and money. Defects that are removed early in the process will not cause subsequent defects in derived work products. The cost of quality will be reduced since fewer failures will occur later in the SDLC (Boehm 1981). To find defects early, both static testing and dynamic testing should be started as early as possible.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a project risk?
options: The design is not optimized for mobile devices, leading to slow loading times
Test cases are poorly written, making it difficult to verify requirements effectively
Features have limited value to the user
Late changes in scope cause significant rework and delay the project schedule
explanation:
d) is correct. Project risks include:

  • Organizational issues (e.g., delays in work products deliveries, inaccurate estimates, cost-cutting)

  • People issues (e.g., insufficient skills, conflicts, communication problems, shortage of staff)

  • Technical issues (e.g., scope creep, poor tool support)

  • Supplier issues (e.g., third-party delivery failure, bankruptcy of the supporting company)

Options a) and c) are product risks; b) is a quality risk of the testware.

stem:
User Story:

  • As a user, I want to be able to search for restaurants by cuisine type on a food discovery app, so that I can easily find dining options that match my taste preferences.

Acceptance Criteria:

  • The filter should allow the user to select one or more cuisine types
  • The search results should update dynamically as the user selects different cuisine types
  • The filter should work on all supported platforms (iOS, Android, Web)

Precondition:

  • There are only two restaurants available in the app: Restaurant X offers Italian cuisine, and Restaurant Y offers Chinese cuisine.

Which of the following is the BEST example of a test case which would be executed FIRST?
options: Enter the app and set the filter to show only Italian cuisine. Expected result: results show Restaurant X only. Change the cuisine filter to Chinese. Expected result: results now include only Restaurant Y

Enter the app. Expected result: the default filter is set to 'All Cuisines.' Add Restaurant Z offering French cuisine to the database. Refresh the app. Expected result: the default filter updates to include French cuisine

Enter the app and set the filter to show Italian cuisine. Expected result: results show Restaurant X. Then, change the app's language setting from English to Spanish. Expected result: all interface texts, including the cuisine filter options, change to Spanish

Enter the app on different devices: iPhone, Android phone, and a web browser on a laptop. Set the filter to show Chinese cuisine on all devices. Expected result: Restaurant Y is displayed on all platforms
explanation: a) is correct. This test case directly tests the core acceptance criteria, verifying that the app allows the user to filter restaurants by cuisine type and updates the search results dynamically based on the selection. Typically, the first test cases are positive, confirming the correct behavior without exceptions or error conditions. After the positive test cases are done, the team should perform negative testing. Finally, the team should cover non-functional quality characteristics.

stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding system testing?
options: System testing focuses on the overall behavior and capabilities of an entire system or product, often including functional testing of end-to-end tasks and the non-functional testing of quality characteristics

The main purpose of system testing is to instill confidence that the system will remain operational and can recover swiftly from adverse events, all without introducing additional risk to the production environment
The main purpose of system testing is to build confidence that the system is in conformance with the contract or regulations

The focus of system testing is validation, assessing how well the system performs in real-world scenarios and its suitability for deployment or actual use by its intended users, rather than primarily detecting defects
explanation:
a) is correct. System testing focuses on the overall behavior and capabilities of an entire system or product, often including functional testing of end-to-end tasks and non-functional testing of quality characteristics.

Note: b) describes operational acceptance testing; c) describes contractual/regulatory acceptance testing; d) describes user acceptance testing (alpha/beta).

stem: A tester is preparing a report outlining the testing activities planned for the next iteration. This information is most likely to be included in:
options: Risk assessment report
Test completion report
Test progress report
Test strategy document
explanation: c) is correct. The test progress report outlines the current status and plans for upcoming testing activities.

stem: Which of the following would be considered a form of static analysis, as described in the text?
options: Examining code coverage reports to identify untested areas
Running automated regression tests after a new software build
Using a tool to check for inconsistent variable naming conventions in the code
Observing user behavior during a usability testing session
explanation: c) is correct. Code, process specification, system architecture specification or other work products are evaluated through manual examination (e.g., reviews) or with the help of a tool (e.g., static analysis). While largely used to detect specific code defects, static analysis is also used to evaluate maintainability and security. Spelling checkers and readability tools are other examples of static analysis tools.

stem: Mind mapping is a collaborative technique well-suited for user story writing. Which of these activities is it MOST helpful for?
options: Prioritizing user stories based on business value
Creating detailed technical design specifications
Identifying relationships between user stories and potential dependencies
Developing test cases and test scenarios
explanation: c) is correct. The visual nature of mind maps helps uncover how different features or aspects of a user story might connect and impact each other.

stem: Your project involves creating an IoT device for smart homes that can control lighting, heating, and security systems. The team is currently integrating the security system feature. Which of the following would be a test analysis activity for this feature?
options: Calculating the effort required to test the security system integration with the overall smart home ecosystem
Determining the security scenarios that need to be tested, such as unauthorized access and data encryption
Selecting a set of static analysis tools to find vulnerabilities in the code base of the security system
Analyzing the results of security system tests to identify any patterns in the failures that occurred
explanation: b) is correct. Test analysis includes analyzing the test basis to identify testable features and to define and prioritize associated test conditions, together with the related risks and risk levels. The test basis and the test objects are also evaluated to identify defects they may contain and to assess their testability. Test analysis is often supported by the use of test techniques. Test analysis answers the question "what to test?" in terms of measurable coverage criteria.

stem: In a DevOps pipeline, how does configuration management support continuous integration and continuous delivery/deployment?
options: By automating the creation of test cases
By ensuring that only approved changes are deployed to production
By tracking the number of defects found during testing
By generating test reports
explanation: b) is correct. This is the core of how CM supports CI/CD. CM tools track and control changes, ensuring that only validated and approved configurations move through the pipeline.

stem:
The system for selling cinema tickets calculates the discount type based on the client's birth year (BY) and on the current year (CY) as follows:

Let D be the difference between CY and BY, that is, D = CY – BY.

  • If D < 16 then apply child discount (...; 16)
  • If 16 ≤ D < 21 then apply the student discount [16; 21)
  • If 20 < D ≤ 59 then apply no discount (20; 59]
  • If D ≥ 60 then apply the pensioner discount [60;...)

Your test suite already contains two test cases:

  • BY = 2022, CY = 2023, expected result: child discount
  • BY = 1950, CY = 2023, expected result: pensioner discount

Which TWO of the following test data sets should be added to achieve full valid equivalence partitioning coverage for the discount type?
explanation: c) is correct. CY – BY = 21, 16 so these inputs correspond to the not yet covered "no discount" partition and "student discount" partition. The existing test cases already cover the child discount (D=1) and pensioner discount (D=73) partitions.

stem:
Which of the below tests are executed as regression tests and which as confirmation tests?

  1. Regression testing
  2. Confirmation testing

a. Running automation tests on the entire system environment to ensure that recent changes or fixes in the production environment have not introduced new defects in previously stable features b. Running automation tests of the filter feature that had been "passed" after the fix for the sorting feature c. Testing to ensure that users who couldn't log into the system can now log in after the fix in the login functionality d. Running automation tests of the sorting feature that had been "failed" due to the defect in products, after the fix of those products
explanation:
d) is correct.

  • a-1: Assesses the whole system to check if recent modifications negatively affected any stable features, a core objective of regression testing.

  • b-1: Evaluates if a fix in one feature (sorting) has impacted another feature (filter), aligning with regression testing goals to detect indirect impacts of changes.

  • c-2: Directly verifies that a specific defect (login issues) has been resolved, fitting the definition of confirmation testing.

  • d-2: Focuses on confirming that the repair of a known defect in the sorting feature has corrected the issue, typical of confirmation testing.

stem: During the 'Individual Review' phase, what is the main activity?
options: Evaluating the review findings against the exit criteria to make a review decision
Communicating defects to the appropriate person or team
Applying review techniques to identify anomalies, recommendations, and questions
Analyzing potential defects, assigning ownership and status to them
explanation: c) is correct. Individual review: Every reviewer performs an individual review to assess the quality of the work product under review, and to identify anomalies, recommendations, and questions by applying one or more review techniques (e.g., checklist-based reviewing, scenario-based reviewing). The ISO/IEC 20246 standard provides more depth on different review techniques. The reviewers log all their identified anomalies, recommendations, and questions.

stem: In the 'Test implementation' activity, what testware is NOT produced as the output?
options: A sequence of test cases in execution order, and any associated actions that may be required to set up the initial preconditions and any wrap up activities post execution
A set of test scripts or test procedures to be executed in a specific test run
Documentation of the goal or objective for a test session
A schedule for the execution of test suites within a test cycle
explanation: c) is correct. Documentation of the goal or objective for a test session is a test charter, which is produced during test execution (for exploratory testing sessions), not during test implementation. Test implementation produces: test suites (a), test procedures/scripts (b), and test execution schedules (d).

stem:
You want to estimate the test effort for the new project using estimation based on ratios. You calculate the test-to-development effort ratio using averaged data for both development effort and test effort from five historical projects similar to the new one. The table shows this historical data:

The estimated development effort for the new project is 400 person-days.

What is your estimate of the test effort in this project?
options: 50 person-days
100 person-days
200 person-days
300 person-days
explanation: b) is correct. The average development effort is 200 person-days and the average test effort is 50 person-days (calculated from the five projects). The average test-to-development effort ratio is 1:4 (50 : 200), which means that historically, on average, the test effort is 25% of the development effort. So if the development effort is estimated to be 400 person-days, the estimated test effort is: 25% × 400 = 0.25 × 400 = 100 person-days.

stem: When considering the implementation of test automation, which of the following factors poses the LEAST significant risk?
options: Misalignment between test automation goals and business objectives, leading to wasted resources
Implementing automation in testing will immediately double the software development budget
Underutilization of test automation due to a lack of training and familiarity with the tools among staff
Selecting automation tools that are not well-suited to the application's technology stack
explanation: b) is correct. This is an unrealistic claim, not a genuine risk factor. While test automation does involve costs, it does not "immediately double" the software development budget. The other options (misaligned goals, underutilization due to lack of training, unsuitable tools) are real, significant risks of test automation.

stem:
A company has set up an employee wellness program and combined it with the payment for health insurance:

The program has the following rules:

  1. Employees who consume 0 units or less of alcohol per week get $50 off their payment
  2. Employees who consume 20 units or less of alcohol per week get $25 off their payment
  3. Employees who consume 40 units or less of alcohol per week get $10 off their payment
  4. Employees who consume more than 40 units of alcohol per week get $0 off their payment

Using two-value boundary value analysis, which of the following sets of test inputs provides the highest level of boundary value coverage?
explanation:
c) is correct. All valid values for 2-value BVA. The equivalence classes are:

  • (a1) units per week = 0 → [0]

  • (a2) 1 ≤ units per week ≤ 20 → [1; 20]

  • (a3) 21 ≤ units per week ≤ 40 → [21; 40]

  • (a4) units per week ≥ 41 → [41; ...]

2-value BVA: (a1) min: 0, max+1: 1; (a2) min: 1, max: 20, max+1: 21; (a3) min: 21, max: 40, max+1: 41; (a4) min: 41. This gives the set {0, 1, 20, 21, 40, 41}.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical responsibility of the test management role?
options: Conducting exploratory testing to uncover unexpected issues and defects
Analyzing project requirements and translating them into comprehensive test plans
Updating documentation, including test plans and procedures, to reflect any changes or insights gained during the testing process
Managing communication channels to provide stakeholders with timely updates on test status, issues, and resolutions
explanation: a) is correct. Conducting exploratory testing is an example of test execution, which is a tester's responsibility, not a test management responsibility. Test management typically includes: test planning (b), maintaining test documentation (c), and stakeholder communication (d).

stem: The team has recently concluded a retrospective, during which they discussed what was successful and should be retained, as well as how to incorporate the improvements and retain the successes in the future. Which of the following is not an example of the topics they most probably discussed to identify process improvements?
options: Why did regression testing take longer than expected?
Which of the developers does not perform the code review, which is why the features get into testing late?
Why the team's velocity is twice as low as before?
How can the test environment be improved and improved to make it more stable?
explanation: b) is correct. Retrospectives focus on process improvements, not on blaming individuals. Identifying which specific developer is responsible for problems goes against the collaborative, no-blame spirit of retrospectives. The other options discuss process-related topics suitable for retrospective discussion.

stem:
You are testing a popular language-learning platform that offers a range of courses to help users learn different languages. The platform uses a gamified approach to language education, making the learning process engaging and interactive. You need to execute test cases from the regression test suite in accordance with the specified execution schedule. Consider the following list of test cases, severities and coverages:

You aim to prioritize test cases using coverage-based prioritization, wherein the test execution sequence is determined by coverage of the single test case. In case the coverage percentage achieved by test cases is the same, the test case with the highest severity is executed first.

Which test case should be executed as the LAST one?
options: TC1
TC2
TC5
TC6
explanation: b) is correct. As the question asks about 'coverage-based prioritization' and NOT 'additional coverage-based prioritization,' you simply need to calculate the original coverage—nothing more. Execution Order: 1. TC3 is run first → Coverage 35%, Priority High 2. TC4 is run second → Coverage 35%, Priority Low 3. TC1 is run third → Coverage 30%, Priority Low 4. TC5 is run fourth → Coverage 30%, Priority Very Low 5. TC6 is run fifth → Coverage 25%, Priority High 6. TC2 is run sixth (LAST) → Coverage 25%, Priority Medium

stem:
The following decision table contains the rules for determining the risk of atherosclerosis.

Which test case will show that there are contradictory rules in the decision table?
options: TC: Cholesterol = 140 (mg/dl); Blood pressure = 125 (mm Hg)
TC: Cholesterol = 124 (mg/dl); Blood pressure = 140 (mm Hg)
TC: Cholesterol = 125 (mg/dl); Blood pressure = 140 (mm Hg)
TC: Cholesterol = 201 (mg/dl); Blood pressure = 140 (mm Hg)
explanation: c) is correct. With Cholesterol = 125 and Blood pressure = 140, the input matches multiple rules with conflicting actions (e.g., Rule 2 with Cholesterol ≤ 124 boundary interpretation and Rule 3 with Cholesterol 125–200 and BP ≤ 140), revealing contradictory rules in the decision table.

stem:
A defect arises not purely from the software or the hardware but from their interaction, such as a timing issue where the software expects a response from the hardware within a certain timeframe that isn't always met.

Which of the following skills is MOST important for a software tester to have in order to effectively identify the defect in software application?
options: Technical knowledge
Domain knowledge
Thoroughness, carefulness, curiosity, attention to details, being methodical
Analytical thinking, critical thinking, creativity
explanation: a) is correct. While being generic, the following skills are particularly relevant for testers: Technical knowledge (to increase efficiency of testing, e.g., by using appropriate test tools). For a defect arising from software-hardware interaction (timing issues), technical knowledge is essential to understand and diagnose the problem.

stem:
You have received the following defect report from the testing team stating that the anomaly described is causing significant disruptions:

'Application crash on file upload'

2023-April-15 – Jane Smith The application crashes when uploading files larger than 5MB using the document upload feature on the data management page. Reproduced the issue using standard test files 'Test_Doc_10MB.pdf' and 'Test_Doc_6MB.jpg' in the Staging test v2.4.1. The application should manage file uploads without crashing, according to the feature specifications. This issue has been marked as high priority due to its impact on daily operations, as outlined in REQ-1023.

What critical information is MISSING from this test report that would have been useful for the developers?
options: Severity of the defect and expected result
Test environment and application version
References to test cases and defect status
Priority of the fix and description of the failure
explanation: c) is correct. The report lacks explicit references to specific test cases that verify the feature, which could help in assessing the scope of testing and understanding the background of the testing process. Moreover, while the report mentions the priority, it does not specify the current status of the defect (like open, under review, etc.), which is critical for tracking and management purposes.

stem:
Your goal is to test the new feature with cookies introduced in the login functionality of the system.

Every time the user changes the login type, the cookies should be cleared automatically. Also, if the cookies expire and the user tries to open the dashboard page, then the user is automatically redirected to the login page

Consider the following state transition diagram for a login system:

Assume that you want to develop the minimum number of tests to cover each valid transition in the state transition diagram. Assume further that each test must start at the beginning state, LOGIN, and each test case ends when a transition arrives at the beginning state.

How many tests cases do you need?
explanation:
c) is correct. The 6 test cases covering all valid transitions:

  • TC1: Continue with Phone, Back

  • TC2: Continue with Email, Back

  • TC3: Continue with Social Media, Back

  • TC4: Continue with Phone, Valid code, Reload page [valid cookies], Reload page [expired cookies]

  • TC5: Continue with Email, Valid code, Reload page [expired cookies]

  • TC6: Continue with Social Media, Valid password, Reload page [expired cookies]

stem: Which of the following is NOT promoted by Continuous Integration (CI) in DevOps?
options: Encouraging developers to submit high-quality code accompanied by component tests and static analysis
Discouraging testers to perform testing manually
Facilitating the establishment of stable test environments
Minimizing the risk in regression due to the scale and range of automated regression tests
explanation:
b) is correct. From the testing perspective, some of the benefits of DevOps are:

  • Fast feedback on the code quality, and whether changes adversely affect existing code

  • CI promotes a shift-left approach in testing by encouraging developers to submit high quality code accompanied by component tests and static analysis

  • Promotes automated processes like CI/CD that facilitate establishing stable test environments

  • Increases the view on non-functional quality characteristics (e.g., performance, reliability)

  • Automation through a delivery pipeline reduces the need for repetitive manual testing

CI does NOT discourage manual testing - it reduces the need for repetitive manual testing, but manual testing (e.g., exploratory testing) remains valuable.

End of Sample Exam IX - Quiz 15 (40 questions)

stem: How does quality assurance (QA) differ from testing in terms of their approach?
options: QA is product-oriented, while testing is process-oriented
QA is reactive, while testing is proactive
QA is preventive, while testing is corrective
QA is focused on achieving appropriate levels of quality, while testing focuses on implementing and improving processes
explanation: c) is correct. Per syllabus. QA is a process-oriented, preventive approach that focuses on the implementation and improvement of processes. It works on the basis that if a good process is followed correctly, then it will generate a good product. QA applies to both the development and testing processes, and is the responsibility of everyone on a project. Testing is a product-oriented, corrective approach that focuses on those activities supporting the achievement of appropriate levels of quality.

stem: Which of the following options does not represent a good testing practice?
options: Testers are involved in reviewing work products as soon as drafts of this documentation are available
Different test levels have specific and different test objectives
Testers should automate the regression tests of the previous phase as soon as the deployment is successful
Test analysis and design for a given test level begins during the corresponding development phase of the SDLC
explanation: c) is correct. Waiting until after deployment to automate regression tests is too late - regression tests should be automated as early as possible (e.g., during the test level itself, not after deployment). The other options are good testing practices: early reviewer involvement (a), distinct test level objectives (b), and early test analysis/design alongside development (d).

stem: Why is frequent stakeholder feedback important?
options: It reduces the workload of the project team
It facilitates early communication of potential quality issues
It allows stakeholders to change the project scope frequently
It eliminates the need for project management
explanation: b) is correct. Obtaining feedback from stakeholders early and often in the software development process can be highly beneficial as it facilitates early communication of potential quality issues, can prevent misunderstandings about requirements, and ensures that any changes in stakeholder requirements are understood and implemented sooner.

stem: In the context of test techniques, what is the main difference between white-box and black-box testing?
options: White-box testing requires no prior knowledge of the software's internal workings
Black-box testing designs test cases based on the internal structure of the software
White-box testing focuses on the specified behavior of the software without considering its internal workings
Black-box testing is based on an analysis of the software's specified behavior without reference to its internal structure
explanation: d) is correct. Black-box testing (functional/non-functional) is based on an analysis of the specified behavior of the software without reference to its internal structure. White-box testing, in contrast, derives test cases from the internal structure/processing of the software.

stem:
A software team is analyzing the following data points:

  • The percentage of requirements covered by test cases
  • The percentage of code lines executed during testing
  • The number of decision points exercised by tests

Which metric category do these techniques belong to?
options: Project Progress Metrics
Product Quality Metrics
Coverage Metrics
Risk Metrics
explanation: c) is correct. According to the syllabus: Coverage metrics (e.g., requirements coverage, code coverage).

stem: Which activities below best represent responsibilities that are consistent with agile development's Whole Team approach?
options: Testers are responsible for developing unit tests which they pass on to the developers for testing
Business representatives are expected to select the tools the team will use during the project
Testers are expected to work with customer representatives to create acceptance tests
Developers are expected to test non-functional requirements (performance, usability, security, etc.)
explanation: c) is correct. Testers support & collaborate with business representatives to help them create suitable acceptance tests.

stem: Which statement accurately describes the difference between branch coverage and statement coverage?
options: Statement coverage requires more test cases to be executed than branch coverage
Branch coverage ensures that every possible branch is executed, while statement coverage ensures all executable statements in the code are exercised
Branch coverage is a subset of statement coverage
Statement coverage measures the execution of decision points, whereas branch coverage does not
explanation: b) is correct. Branch coverage ensures that every possible branch (outcome of decision points) is executed, while statement coverage ensures all executable statements in the code are exercised. 100% branch coverage guarantees 100% statement coverage (not the reverse), so branch coverage subsumes statement coverage.

stem:
Your team has defined three test levels in the test approach:

  • Unit testing
  • Component integration testing
  • System testing

Which of the following is BEST suited to be the exit criterion for system testing?
options: The user stories selected for the iteration are complete and have testable acceptance criteria
The fail-pass ratio for end-to-end tests of user stories, features, and functions is 5:95
The critical defects within the components and interfaces among units have been successfully addressed and resolved
The production-like environment, encompassing all necessary hardware and software for all supported configurations, has been established
explanation: b) is correct. A fail-pass ratio for end-to-end tests is an appropriate exit criterion for system testing. Option a) is an entry criterion (testable acceptance criteria), c) is an exit criterion for component integration testing, and d) is an entry criterion (test environment readiness).

stem:
Which of the following statements about Acceptance Test-Driven Development (ATDD) is true?

  • i. User stories need to include acceptance tests, which can then be transformed into acceptance criteria
  • ii. ATDD tests could be, and usually are, automated for ease of use
  • iii. ATDD tests belong to quadrant one (Q1) and are technology-facing
  • iv. ATDD tests belong to quadrant two (Q2) and are business-facing
  • v. ATDD tests can't be automated
options: i, ii, iv
ii, iv
ii, iii
iv, v
explanation:
b) is correct.

  • i. False. User stories are meant to be high-level descriptions of a feature from the user's perspective. During ATDD's collaborative sessions, acceptance criteria are derived from these user stories, not the tests themselves.

  • ii. True. A significant benefit of ATDD is the ability to automate acceptance tests, providing rapid feedback as development progresses. Automation makes these tests a core part of regression testing suites.

  • iii. False. Quadrant 1 (Q1) tests in the Agile Testing Quadrant typically focus on unit-level, developer-centric tests. ATDD tests are higher-level and focus on the business-facing perspective.

  • iv. True. ATDD tests belong to Quadrant 2 (Q2) and are business-facing.

  • v. False. ATDD tests can be automated.

stem: Which of the following best describes a limitation of white-box testing?
options: It can only be applied to clear and distinct requirements and specifications
It can be time-consuming and complex
It may not detect defects resulting from omitted requirements
It is only applicable during the final stages of testing
explanation: c) is correct. White-box testing is based on the code's internal structure, so if a requirement is omitted (missing functionality not implemented), there is no code to analyze and the defect cannot be detected by white-box techniques. This is why black-box testing based on requirements is also needed.

stem:
You're testing a new data migration tool designed to transfer user data from an old system to a new one. During testing, you discover that the tool consistently fails to migrate a specific data field for a subset of users. The developer diagnosed the defect as a problem with data mapping for the specific data field. The code responsible for mapping that field to the new system was missing a specific case statement to handle the data format used by a subset of users in the old system.

Which of the following correctly describes a problem with data mapping for the specific data field?
options: The failed migrations of a specific data field for a subset of users by the tool is an error
The failed migrations of a specific data field for a subset of users by the tool is a defect
A problem with data mapping for the specific data field is a root cause
A problem with data mapping for the specific data field is a defect
explanation: d) is correct. It is an example of the defect in the code. Defects can be found in documentation, such as a requirements specification or a test script, in source code, or in a supporting artifact such as a build file. Defects in artifacts produced earlier in the SDLC, if undetected, often lead to defective artifacts later in the lifecycle. (The failed migrations observed during testing are failures; the missing case statement in the code is the defect.)

stem: According to the testing quadrants model, which of the following falls into Quadrant Q4?
options: System testing
Performance testing
Usability testing
Regression testing
explanation: b) is correct, according to the syllabus 5.1.7. Testing Quadrants. Quadrant Q1 contains component and component integration tests; Quadrant Q2 contains functional tests, examples, user story tests, user experience prototypes, API testing, and simulations; Quadrant Q3 contains exploratory testing, usability testing, user acceptance testing; Quadrant Q4 contains smoke tests and non-functional tests (except usability tests).

stem: Which of the following best describes the documentation process in Session-Based Exploratory Testing?
options: Detailed test scripts are written in advance and strictly followed during the test sessions
Documentation is not required in Exploratory Testing to allow for greater flexibility
Testers may use test session sheets to document what was tested, observations, and insights
Only the final test results are documented for stakeholder review, without detailing the testing process
explanation: c) is correct. Exploratory testing is sometimes conducted using session-based testing to structure the testing. The tester may use test session sheets to document the steps followed and the discoveries made.

stem: Which of these statements does NOT support effective reviews?
options: Providing actionable feedback to authors and other stakeholders
Always conduct two reviews, one to search for defects, the other to emphasize the positive aspects of the object under review and its author
Ensuring participants have the appropriate technical knowledge
Tracking progress in addressing issues raised during the review
explanation: b) is correct. Conducting two separate reviews (one for defects, one for positives) is not a recognized factor for effective reviews. Effective reviews involve finding defects while providing constructive feedback in a single review, along with appropriate participant knowledge and issue tracking.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a primary concern when implementing test automation in software testing processes?
options: Underestimating the time needed to train the team on the tool
Over-reliance on automation, potentially neglecting critical thinking
Difficulties in maintaining scripts if the application under test changes
Testers losing all motivation because automation does the work for them
explanation: d) is correct. Test automation does not cause testers to lose all motivation - testers remain essential for critical thinking, test design, and exploratory testing. The primary concerns of test automation include: underestimating training time (a), over-reliance on automation (b), and script maintenance difficulties (c).

stem: Which of the following statements about checklist-based testing is true?
options: It is the best technique for uncovering performance-related defects
Checklists should include items that can be easily checked through automation
Testers should be discouraged from going beyond the checklist's scope
Checklists can be derived from knowledge about what is important for the user
explanation: d) is correct. Per Certified Tester Foundation Level Syllabus 4.4.3. Checklist-Based Testing: In checklist-based testing, a tester designs, implements, and executes tests to cover test conditions from a checklist. Checklists can be built based on experience, knowledge about what is important for the user, or an understanding of why and how software fails.

stem:
A development team has defined two main testing objectives: verifying that a test object complies with regulatory requirements and validating whether the test object is complete and works as expected by the stakeholders. The verification process will be done by an independent testing team. For validation, it was decided to use two forms of acceptance testing, such as alpha testing and beta testing, to involve the end-users in testing as early as possible.

Which testing principle explains the desire to involve end-users in testing in addition to the testing team testing for validation purposes?
options: Early testing saves time and money
Absence-of-defects fallacy
Testing is context dependent
Exhaustive testing is impossible
explanation: b) is correct. The absence-of-defects fallacy states that a system may pass all tests (appear defect-free) but still be unusable if it does not fulfill the users' needs. This explains why end-users are involved in validation (alpha/beta testing) in addition to the testing team - to ensure the system actually meets user expectations, not just that it is defect-free.

stem: Which of the following statements about product risk analysis is TRUE?
options: The risk level is always calculated using a risk matrix
Risk identification involves generating a comprehensive list of risks
All risks identified are typically accepted without mitigation
It focuses solely on external factors affecting the project
explanation: b) is correct. Risk identification is described in the syllabus as the process of generating a comprehensive list of risks using various techniques and tools, such as brainstorming, workshops, interviews, and cause-effect diagrams.

stem:
Consider this acceptance criterion for a user story on an e-commerce site, presented in a table:

In what format is this acceptance criteria written?
options: Rule-oriented
Scenario-oriented
Product-oriented
Decision table
explanation: a) is correct. The rule-oriented format includes formats like bullet point verification lists or tabulated forms of input-output mappings, explicitly showing the rules to be followed. Given/When/Then is a scenario-oriented format because it describes a scenario to be verified.

stem: Which statement correctly describes functional testing?
options: Functional tests are based on the functions, which are typically described in work products such as business requirements specifications, functional specifications, use cases, epics, or user stories
Functional testing focuses on the functionality of a system, which informally is testing how well the system does what it does
Functional testing is exclusively carried out at the system level or at lower test levels within the software development lifecycle
The primary objective of functional testing is to check performance efficiency, security vulnerabilities, and system compatibility
explanation: a) is correct. Functional testing is based on functions described in work products like requirements specifications, use cases, epics, or user stories. Informally, functional testing tests "what" the system does (not "how well" - that's non-functional). It can occur at all test levels, and d) describes non-functional testing.

stem: Which of the following statements about product risk analysis is FALSE?
options: Risk identification is based on historical data and stakeholders' subjective judgments
Risk assessment can use both quantitative and qualitative methods
Stakeholders can identify risks using techniques such as workshops and interviews
The results of product risk analysis determine the scope of testing efforts
explanation: a) is correct (the FALSE statement). This statement can be misleading if interpreted to imply that risk identification is exclusively or always based on historical data and subjective judgments. While these sources can contribute to risk identification, it also commonly includes techniques like brainstorming, cause-effect diagrams, and the experience and insights from various stakeholders, not strictly historical data and subjective judgments alone.

stem:
Decide which of the following statements (i-v) are true for dynamic testing and which are true for static testing

  • i. It can be applied to the unit testing level
  • ii. Identifying unmaintainable code is easier with this testing
  • iii. Defects can be identified with this testing
  • iv. Can be applied to non-executable work products
  • v. Can be used to measure performance efficiency
options: i, ii, iii, iv are true for static testing; iii, v are true for dynamic testing
i, ii, iii, iv are true for static testing; i, iii, v are true for dynamic testing
i, ii, iii, iv are true for static testing; i, v are true for dynamic testing
i, ii, iii, iv are true for static testing; v is true for dynamic testing
explanation:
b) is correct.

  • Static testing: can be applied at unit level (i), easier to identify unmaintainable code (ii), can identify defects (iii), applies to non-executable work products (iv)

  • Dynamic testing: can be applied at unit level (i), can identify defects (iii), can measure performance efficiency (v - requires execution)

stem:
An employee's bonus is to be calculated. It cannot be negative, but it can be calculated down to zero. The bonus is based on the length of employment:

  • Less than or equal to 2 years
  • More than 2 years but less than 5 years
  • 5 to 10 years inclusively
  • Longer than 10 years

For additional factors, gifts of various values with the company logo are provided:

  • If the employee participated in conferences on behalf of the company - Hoodie
  • If the employee participated in the training of junior employees - a jacket

You want to apply the Each Choice Equivalence Partitioning test technique but you also want to test each partition separately.

How many partitions do you need to cover?
explanation:
c) is correct. The equivalence classes are:

  • Length of employment (4 classes): (a1) 0 ≤ time ≤ 2 [0; 2]; (a2) 2 < time < 5 (2; 5); (a3) 5 ≤ time ≤ 10 [5; 10]; (a4) time > 10 (10; ...)

  • Participation in conferences (2 classes): (b1) No; (b2) Yes

  • Participation in training (2 classes): (c1) No; (c2) Yes

Total: 4 + 2 + 2 = 8 partitions. The question asks about the number of partitions, not the number of test cases.

stem:
Which of the following factors (i-v) have SIGNIFICANT influence on the test process?

  • i. Changing the SDLC from Scrum to Waterfall
  • ii. Merger of two organizations with identical processes
  • iii. Increasing the number of members in the testing team
  • iv. Obsolescence of load testing tools
  • v. End users skills, knowledge, level of experience, availability, training needs
options: i, ii, iii, iv have significant influence; v has not
i, iii, iv have significant influence; ii, v have not
i, iii, iv, v have significant influence; ii has not
i, ii, iii, iv, v have significant influence;
explanation: b) is correct. Changing the SDLC (i), team size changes (iii), and tool obsolescence (iv) significantly influence the test process. A merger of organizations with identical processes (ii) has no significant impact since the processes remain the same. End users' skills (v) do not directly influence the test process itself.

stem: Which of the following statements about 'Configuration Management' is TRUE?
options: Configuration Management allows changes to the baseline without any formal process
Configuration Management includes identifying, controlling, and tracking configuration items such as test plans and test results
Configuration Management primarily deals with financial tracking within the testing process
Configuration Management eliminates the need for version control in testing environments
explanation: b) is correct. Configuration Management is crucial for the systematic handling of test artifacts, where it identifies, controls, and tracks configuration items including test plans, strategies, cases, and results to ensure consistency and traceability in the testing process.

stem:
You are testing a thermostat for a heating/air conditioning system. You have been given the following requirements:

The developer made a mistake in the first equivalence partition, instead of (number of units ≤ -1) developer coded (number of units = -1)

Using three-value boundary value analysis, which of the following sets of test inputs provides the highest level of boundary value coverage?
explanation: c) is correct. The 3-value BVA coverage items are: {–1, 0, 1, 2, 18, 19, 20, 21} → 8 boundary values. Coverage is calculated as: number of covered boundary values / 8. This set covers 5 of 8 boundary values (–1, 0, 1, 19, 21) → 62.5% coverage, which is the highest boundary value coverage among the options. All values are valid three-value BVA boundaries, making this option the best choice.

stem: During maintenance testing, what is the PRIMARY benefit of conducting impact analysis?
options: Ensuring that all defects identified in production are fixed
Validating that a work product matches a stakeholder's needs
Verifying that the software meets the user's requirements
Assessing the feasibility and potential impact of proposed changes on the system
explanation: d) is correct. Impact analysis may be done before a change is made, to help decide if the change should be made, based on the potential consequences in other areas of the system.

stem:
Given the following review types:

  1. Informal Review
  2. Walkthrough
  3. Technical Review
  4. Inspection

And the following descriptions:

A. Led by the author B. The author cannot act as a scribe C. Led by a moderator D. The main objective is to detect anomalies

Which of the following BEST matches the review types and the descriptions?
explanation:
b) is correct.

  • Informal Review (1) = D: The main objective is to detect anomalies

  • Walkthrough (2) = A: Led by the author

  • Technical Review (3) = C: Led by a moderator (technically qualified reviewers)

  • Inspection (4) = B: The author cannot act as a scribe (formal review with defined roles)

stem: What is the MAJOR drawback of NOT having a well-established traceability matrix between the Test Basis and Testware?
options: Difficulty in demonstrating test coverage during audits or reviews
Increased test execution time due to manual requirement verification
Inability to automate test execution based on specific requirements
Reduced communication between testers and developers
explanation: a) is correct. In addition to evaluating coverage, good traceability makes it possible to determine the impact of changes, facilitates test audits, and helps meet IT governance criteria. Good traceability also makes test progress and completion reports more easily understandable by including the status of test basis elements. This can also assist in communicating the technical aspects of testing to stakeholders in an understandable manner. Traceability provides information to assess product quality, process capability, and project progress against business goals.

stem:
You want to estimate the test effort for the new project using estimation based on ratios. You calculate the test-to-development effort ratio using averaged data for both development effort and test effort from four historical projects similar to the new one. The table shows this historical data:

The estimated development effort for the new project is 2,000 person days.

What is your estimate of the test effort in this project?
options: 100 person-days
200 person-days
400 person-days
500 person-days
explanation: c) is correct. The average development effort is 500 and the average test effort is 100 (calculated from the four projects). The average test-to-development effort ratio is 1:5 (100 : 500), which means that historically, on average, the test effort is 20% of the development effort. So if the development effort is estimated to be 2,000, the estimated test effort is: 20% × 2,000 = 0.2 × 2,000 = 400.

stem: Which type of tools is essential for facilitating communication among team members during the test process?
options: Management tools
Collaboration tools
Static testing tools
DevOps tools
explanation: b) is correct. Collaboration tools – facilitate communication.

stem:
The following decision table contains the rules for determining the risk of atherosclerosis.

Based on the description of the risk of atherosclerosis, which of the following statements is true?
options: R1, R2, can be merged into a single column
R3, R5, can be merged into a single column
R4, R6, can be merged into a single column
R4, R8, can be merged into a single column
explanation: d) is correct. R4 and R8 can be merged as the actions are the same and the conditions do not conflict in a way that would necessitate separate columns. Both cases indicate a patient with high blood pressure and no medications, where cholesterol level is high but the specific range does not alter the prescribed action.

stem: Typical tasks performed during this, one of the main test activities of the test process, involve identifying and prioritizing test conditions, which can be supported with test design techniques:
options: Acceptance criteria validation for testability
Test design
Test analysis
Backlog Grooming
explanation: c) is correct. Test analysis is likely to involve the use of test techniques to identify test conditions.

stem: Which of the following statements about retrospectives is true?
options: Retrospectives are often held at the end of an iteration to cover topics such as the process, people, organizations, relationships, and tools
Retrospectives are often held at the start of an iteration, to avoid organization mistakes made in the previous iteration
Retrospectives occur every day when all the team members are present typically lasting about 15–20 minutes
Retrospectives are often held at the end of the week to cover topics such as the process, people, organizations, relationships, and tools
explanation: a) is correct. Retrospectives are held at the end of each iteration (not the start, not daily - that's a stand-up, and not weekly) to cover topics such as the process, people, organizations, relationships, and tools.

stem:
You are testing a mobile payment and digital wallet service. It allows users to make secure and contactless payments in stores, online, and within apps using their devices. You need to execute test cases from the negative regression test suite in accordance with the specified execution schedule. Consider the following list of test cases, priorities (i.e., a smaller number means a higher priority) and dependencies:

Which of the following test execution schedules BEST considers the priorities and logical dependency?
explanation: d) is correct. The execution order respects both priorities and dependencies: TC 005 (priority 1, no dependencies) runs first; TC 002 (priority 2) runs second; TC 003 (priority 3, depends on TC 002 ✓) runs third; TC 001 (priority 1, depends on TC 003 and TC 005 ✓) runs fourth; TC 006 (priority 2, depends on TC 002 ✓) runs fifth; TC 004 (priority 4, no dependencies) runs last.

stem:
You need to test the customer support system. The user starts in the OPEN with the user account and has the ability to log into the admin account on certain states of the ticket.

Consider the following state transition diagram for the customer support system:

Assume that you want to develop the minimum number of tests to achieve valid transitions coverage. Assume further that each test must start at the beginning state, OPEN, and each test ends when a transition arrives at the beginning state or in the CLOSED state. How many tests do you need?
explanation:
b) is correct. The 3 test cases covering all valid transitions:

  • TC1: Start progress [user], Stop progress [user], Start progress [user], Resolve [user], Login [user], Close [admin]

  • TC2: Start progress [user], Stop progress [user], Login [user], Reopen [admin]

  • TC3: Start progress [user], Login [user], Reopen [admin]

stem: Which of the following scenarios represents the 'Some independence' testing level?
options: The author of the work product testing their own work
A peer from the same team as the author testing the work product
A tester from a different team within the organization testing the work product
A tester from an external testing company testing the work product
explanation: b) is correct. Work products can be tested by their author (no independence), by the author's peers from the same team (some independence), by testers from outside the author's team but within the organization (high independence), or by testers from outside the organization (very high independence).

stem:
Consider the following defect report:

The "Bulk Upload" feature intermittently fails when processing large data files (1GB or larger) from multiple users simultaneously. According to the new requirements, the system should be able to handle large files smoothly without interruption, but the system failure during file processing is visible in the server logs, and displays the error message to the end user 'Something went wrong'. The anomaly was documented during a load testing session, check the test case ID LT-3229. The operating system used was macOS Catalina, version 10.15.7. The defect is currently open with a priority status of P1.

Which essential information is missing in this defect report?
options: Title with a short summary of the anomaly being reported and author
Status of the defect, references, and date when the anomaly was observed
Date when the anomaly was observed, expected result, and actual result
Unique identifier and Identification of the test object and test environment
Date when the anomaly was observed, unique identifier and author
explanation: e) is correct. The unique identifier for the defect, the author, and the date of the anomaly's observation are missing. The report already includes: description, expected result (per requirements), actual result (error message), test case reference (LT-3229), environment (macOS Catalina), status (open), and priority (P1).

stem:
Consider the following user story:

  • As a library patron, I want to be able to reserve a book online, so that I can pick it up at my convenience

And its acceptance criteria:

    1. The patron can search for books by title, author, or keyword
    1. The patron can see if a book is available for reservation
    1. The patron must be logged in to their library account to place a reservation
    1. Reservations expire after 3 days if not picked up
    1. When a patron arrives to pick up a reserved book, they must log in to the library system to confirm their identity
    1. If login is successful, the librarian can locate the reservation and mark the book as "unavailable"
    1. If login is unsuccessful, the reservation is canceled
    1. The checkout period for a book is 21 days
    1. If a book is returned on or before its due date, the librarian marks it as "available" in the system

Which of the following test cases will NOT be relevant for this user story?
options: Input: The patron searches for a book using the author's name. Expected output: The system displays books matching the search criteria, indicating which are available for reservation
Input: The patron arrives to pick up a reserved book and fails to log in successfully at the library system. Expected output: The system cancels the book reservation
Input: The patron successfully logs in and reserves an available book. Expected output: The reservation is recorded

Input: A patron has not returned a book within the 21-day checkout period. A librarian logs the book back into the system as "overdue." Expected output: The system updates the book's status to "overdue" and may trigger a notification or a fine for the patron.
explanation: d) is correct. The test case is related to overdue books and their handling, which is not discussed in the user story. The user story specifically focuses on a library patron wanting to reserve a book online and the procedures involved in making and managing reservations, not on the penalties or processes for books not returned by their due date.

stem: Which of the following is an example of the shift-left approach?
options: Executing non-functional tests at the system level before the software is accessible to end users
Conducting non-functional tests at the component and component integration levels rather than at the system and system integration levels
Conducting performance, security, and other non-functional testing at the component level when feasible
Involving end users in alpha usability testing when a representative test environment is available
explanation:
c) is correct. The shift-left approach involves performing testing activities earlier in the SDLC. An example is conducting performance, security, and other non-functional testing at the component level when feasible, rather than waiting until later test levels where a complete system is available.

End of Sample Exam X - Quiz 16 (40 questions)

stem: Which of the following statements describes a valid test objective?
options: Triggering failures and causing defects
Initiating errors and identifying root causes
Triggering failures and identifying defects
Debugging failures and finding the root cause
