stem: Which of the following is TRUE regarding the "Branch Coverage"?
options: The branch testing involves designing test cases to exercise branches in the code until an acceptable level of coverage is achieved. Coverage is measured as the number of branches exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of branches and is expressed as a percentage. When 100% branch coverage is achieved, all branches in the code, unconditional and conditional, are exercised by test cases

The branch testing involves designing test cases to exercise statements and branches in the code until an acceptable level of coverage is achieved. Coverage is measured as the number of branches exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of statements and is expressed as a percentage. When 100% branch coverage is achieved, all statements in the code, unconditional and conditional, are exercised by test cases

The branch testing involves designing test cases to exercise branches in the code until an acceptable level of coverage is achieved. Coverage is measured as the number of branches exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of branches and is expressed as a percentage. When 100% branch coverage is achieved, all conditional branches in the code are exercised by test cases

The branch testing involves designing test cases to exercise branches in the code until an acceptable level of coverage is achieved. Coverage is measured as the number of branches exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of branches and is expressed as a percentage. When 100% branch coverage is achieved, all unconditional branches in the code are exercised by test cases
explanation: a) is correct. According to the syllabus: In branch testing the coverage items are branches and the aim is to design test cases to exercise branches in the code until an acceptable level of coverage is achieved. Coverage is measured as the number of branches exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of branches, and is expressed as a percentage. When 100% branch coverage is achieved, all branches in the code, unconditional and conditional, are exercised by test cases.

stem: Which of the following is a typical objective of testing?

stem:

And its acceptance criteria:

  • The user must provide a valid email address (if email is selected) or a valid mobile phone number (if SMS is selected)
  • The user should select the timeframe in which they want to receive notifications (48 hours before departure or 24 hours before departure)
  • The system will send a notification to the user's chosen method if the flight status changes to "delayed" or canceled
  • The user can change their preferred notification method at any time by repeating steps 1-3
  • The user can unsubscribe from notifications immediately after initial subscribing or after changing their notification method

Which of the following test cases will NOT be relevant for this user story?
options: Input: The customer enters a valid flight number, selects SMS as the notification method, and chooses notifications to be sent 48 hours before departure. Expected Output: The system confirms subscription and sends a notification via SMS if there is any change in the flight status.
Input: The customer logs into their account to review past flights they have taken with the airline. Expected Output: The system displays a list of past flight bookings and their details.

Input: The user updates their notification method from SMS to email and selects to receive notifications 24 hours before departure. Expected Output: The system updates the user's preferences and confirms the change.

Input: The user receives an SMS notification for a gate change and then immediately unsubscribes from further notifications. Expected Output: The system processes the unsubscription and confirms that no further notifications will be sent.
explanation: b) is correct. Test case is not relevant to the user story as it deals with reviewing past flight bookings, which is unrelated to receiving real-time notifications for flight delays, cancellations, or gate changes. The user story and its acceptance criteria are focused on the subscription, customization, delivery, and cancellation of real-time notifications, not on historical flight data.

stem: Which of the following is TRUE regarding the "Statement Coverage"?
options: Statement coverage is measured as the number of statements exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of executable statements in the code, and is expressed as a percentage. When 100% statement coverage is achieved, it ensures that all executable statements in the code have been exercised at least once

Statement coverage is measured as the number of branches exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of branches, and is expressed as a percentage. When 100% branch coverage is achieved, all branches in the code, unconditional and conditional, are exercised by test cases

Statement coverage is measured as the number of exercised transitions divided by the total number of transitions, and is expressed as a percentage. Achieving 100% transition coverage guarantees both full all-state coverage and full valid transition coverage and should be a minimum requirement for mission and safety-critical software

Statement coverage is measured as the number of decisions exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of decisions, and is expressed as a percentage. When 100% decision coverage is achieved, all decisions in the code, unconditional and conditional, are exercised by test cases
explanation: a) is correct, according to the syllabus. In statement testing, the coverage items are executable statements. The aim is to design test cases that exercise statements in the code until an acceptable level of coverage is achieved. Coverage is measured as the number of statements exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of executable statements in the code, and is expressed as a percentage. When 100% statement coverage is achieved, it ensures that all executable statements in the code have been exercised at least once.

stem:
You want to estimate the test effort for the new project using estimation based on ratios. You calculate the test-to-development effort ratio using averaged data for both development effort and test effort from four historical projects similar to the new one. The table shows this historical data.

ProjectDev-to-Test Effort Ratio
P13/4

stem: Which of the following is an INVALID objective for testing?

Finding mistakes and triggering errors
Ensuring the required coverage of a test object

explanation: b) is correct. Mistakes and errors are synonyms. Initiating errors is incorrect because testers do not initiate errors, they try to cause failures. Errors are typically made by developers (and cannot really be initiated) and result in defects, which testers attempt to identify either directly through static testing or indirectly through failures with dynamic testing.

stem:

stem:
You are testing a popular online platform that provides information and reviews related to travel, including hotels, restaurants, attractions, and other travel-related businesses. It allows users to browse and read reviews, ratings, and opinions shared by other travelers. In addition to user-generated content, it also provides information on prices, availability, and booking options for hotels and other accommodations. You need to execute test cases from the regression test suite in accordance with the specified execution schedule. Consider the following list of test cases, severities, and coverages:

Test caseCoverageDependency
TC120%
TC210%
TC320%TC2
TC415%
TC525%TC1
TC620%

You aim to prioritize test cases using coverage-based prioritization, wherein the test execution sequence is determined by the coverage of the single test case. In case the coverage percentage achieved by test cases is the same, the test case with the highest severity is executed first.

Given this information, what is the proper order in which to execute these test cases?
options: TC1 - TC5 - TC6 - TC2 - TC3 - TC4
TC1 - TC5 - TC2 - TC3 - TC6 - TC4
TC5 - TC1 - TC6 - TC2 - TC3 - TC4
TC1 - TC5 - TC3 - TC6 - TC4 - TC2
TC5 - TC6 - TC1 - TC2 - TC3 - TC4
explanation: a) is correct. Following the coverage-based prioritization technique, we should execute the test cases that cover the most code first. TC5(25%) - TC1(20%) - TC6(20%) - TC3(20%) - TC4(15%) - TC2(10%); However, TC5 depends on TC1; Thus we need to execute the TC1 first: TC1(20%) - TC5(25%). The next TC can be either TC3 or TC6. TC6 has higher severity, and its dependency is already covered. TC1(20%) - TC5(25%) - TC6(20%). Next we need to run TC3 as it has the highest coverage. However, TC3 depends on TC2; Thus we need to execute the TC2 first. Thus the final order: TC1 - TC5 - TC6 - TC2 - TC3 - TC4.

stem: Which statement regarding the shift-left approach is correct?

Performing non-functional testing starting at the system test level or higher because testers and developers own the environment and can manipulate it to simulate various conditions, thus ensuring that all components interact as expected and meet performance benchmarks
Performing non-functional testing starting at the component test level, where possible

Performing non-functional testing at the alpha testing and beta testing stages with real users allows for valuable feedback on system performance and usability in real-world scenarios, helping to identify and resolve issues before the final release
explanation: c) is correct. According to the syllabus: There are some good practices that illustrate how to achieve a "shift-left" in testing, which include: - Performing non-functional testing starting at the component test level, where possible. stem:

stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE about the relationship between exploratory testing and formal testing techniques?
options: Exploratory testing and formal testing techniques such as black-box or white-box testing cannot be used together in a testing process as they contradict each other's principles and methods
Exploratory testing is generally seen as a replacement for formal testing techniques like black-box and white-box testing because it is entirely based on the tester's experience and intuition

Exploratory testing and formal methods like black-box and white-box testing are only effective when utilized jointly
explanation: c) is correct. According to the syllabus: experience-based test techniques are complementary to the black-box and white-box test techniques. Exploratory testing can incorporate the use of other test techniques (e.g., equivalence partitioning).

stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE about collaborative user story writing?

When dynamic testing identifies a defect, debugging is concerned with finding the causes of this failure (defects), analyzing these causes, and eliminating them
When dynamic testing triggers a failure, debugging is concerned with finding the causes of this failure (defects), analyzing these causes, and eliminating them
explanation: d) is correct. When dynamic testing triggers a failure, debugging is concerned with finding the causes of this failure (defects), analyzing these causes, and eliminating them. When static testing identifies a defect, debugging is concerned with removing it. There is no need for reproduction or diagnosis, since static testing directly finds defects, and cannot cause failures.

stem:
Which of the following items (i-vi) are potential benefits of using test automation?

  • i. Time saved by reducing repetitive manual work
  • ii. Entirely replacing the need for manual testing
  • iii. Automation lowers the required skill level for testers, allowing individuals with minimal technical knowledge to perform complex testing tasks effectively.
  • iv. Test automation guarantees 100% test coverage, ensuring that every possible scenario and edge case is automatically tested without human intervention
  • v. More objective assessment (e.g., coverage) and providing measures that are too complicated for humans to derive
  • vi. Prevention of simple human errors through greater consistency and repeatability
options: i, v, vi
i, iii, v, vi
i, iv, v, vi
i, ii, v, vi
explanation: a) is correct. According to the syllabus: Potential benefits of using test automation include: - Time saved by reducing repetitive manual work (e.g., execute regression tests, re-enter the same test data, compare expected results vs actual results, and check against coding standards) - Prevention of simple human errors through greater consistency and repeatability (e.g., tests are consistently derived from requirements, test data is created in a systematic manner, and tests are executed by a tool in the same order with the same frequency) - More objective assessment (e.g., coverage) and providing measures that are too complicated for humans to derive

stem:
Arrive-and-Go airline wants to clarify its baggage handling policy, whilst maximizing revenues, and will introduce the following tariffs for all baggage per individual customer (weights are rounded up to the nearest 0.1Kg):

  • • The first 6kg will be carried free of charge.
  • • The next 14kg will be carried for a flat charge of $10.
  • • An additional 15kg will be charged a total charge of $25.
  • • Luggage over this amount will be charged a total charge of $50.

The system will automatically assign a value of 0.0 kg for customers who do not check in any luggage, ensuring that all baggage weights are accounted for precisely in the system.

Which of the following sets of test inputs would achieve the BEST VALID equivalence partition coverage?
explanation: c) is correct. 0.0kg(EP1), 14.0kg(EP2), 20.1kg(EP3), 35.1kg(EP4) – 4 partitions (out of 4). This set provides the most efficient coverage by selecting a single value at the start of each partition.

stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE about black-box test techniques?
options: Black-box test techniques (also known as specification-based techniques) are based on an analysis of the specified behavior of the test object without reference to its internal structure and depend on the previous performance outcomes of the software
Black-box test techniques (also known as specification-based techniques) are based on an analysis of the specified behavior of the test object without reference to its internal structure

Black-box test techniques (also known as specification-based techniques) are based on an analysis of the specified behavior of the test object without reference to its internal structure or based on dynamic interactions observed during user operations

Black-box test techniques (also known as specification-based techniques) are based on an analysis of the specified behavior of the test object without reference to its internal structure or based on the information gathered during dynamic testing of the software
explanation: b) is correct. It accurately reflects the definition and purpose of black-box testing, which evaluates the software based on its external specifications and expected functionality without any knowledge of its internal workings.

stem:
Which of the following statements (i–vi) about static testing and dynamic testing are TRUE?

  • i. Static and dynamic testing can both lead to the detection of defects
  • ii. Static testing causes bugs from which the associated defects are determined through subsequent root cause analysis
  • iii. Static testing finds defects directly
  • iv. Dynamic testing can be applied to non-executable work products
  • v. Static testing can be used to measure quality characteristics that are not dependent on executing code (e.g., performance efficiency)
  • vi. Static testing may more easily detect defects that lay on paths through the code that are rarely executed
options: i, iii, vi
iii, vi
i, ii, iii, vi
iii, v, vi
explanation: a) is correct. - (i.) is true, according to the syllabus: Static and dynamic testing (with analysis of failures) can both lead to the detection of defects, however there are some defect types that can only be found by either static or dynamic testing - (iii.) is true, according to the syllabus: Static testing finds defects directly, while dynamic testing causes failures from which the associated defects are determined through subsequent analysis - (vi.) is true, according to the syllabus: Static testing may more easily detect defects that lay on paths through the code that are rarely executed or hard to reach

stem: Choose the statement that correctly reflects one of the testing principles:
options: Testers aim to approximate exhaustive testing by covering as many scenarios as possible
Business people, testers, and developers must work together daily throughout the project
Testing everything (all combinations of inputs and preconditions) is not feasible except for trivial cases
Identifying and fixing all defects guarantees a system meets user needs and expectations
explanation: c) is correct. This directly reflects one of the core testing principles that "exhaustive testing is impossible," noting that testing all possible combinations of inputs and conditions is only feasible in trivial cases. It highlights the impracticality of achieving complete coverage in complex systems and underscores the need for strategic focus in testing efforts.

stem:
Consider the following definitions (1-3) and match the term (A-C) with the definition (1-3):

  • Acceptance criteria are typically created based on the given/when/then format
  • Tests are written first, then the code is written to satisfy the tests, and then the tests and code are refactored
  • Derives tests from acceptance criteria as part of the system design process
  • A. Test-Driven Development (TDD)
  • B. Acceptance Test-Driven Development (ATDD)
  • C. Behavior-Driven Development (BDD)
explanation: a) is correct. According to the syllabus: - TDD: Directs the coding through test cases. Tests are written first, then the code is written to satisfy the tests, and then the tests and code are refactored - ATDD: Derives tests from acceptance criteria as part of the system design process. Tests are written before the part of the application is developed to satisfy the tests - BDD: Expresses the desired behavior of an application with test cases written in a simple form of natural language, which is easy to understand by stakeholders – usually using the Given/When/Then format. Test cases are then automatically translated into executable tests

stem:
Consider the following user story:

• As a library patron, I want to be able to reserve a book online, so that I can pick it up at my convenience

And its acceptance criteria:

  • The patron can search for books by title, author, or keyword
  • The patron can see if a book is available for reservation
  • The patron must be logged in to their library account to place a reservation
  • Reservations expire after 3 days if not picked up
  • When a patron arrives to pick up a reserved book, they must log in to the library system to confirm their identity
  • If login is successful, the librarian can locate the reservation and mark the book as "unavailable"
  • If login is unsuccessful, the reservation is canceled
  • The checkout period for a book is 21 days
  • If a book is returned on or before its due date, the librarian marks it as "available" in the system

Two test cases have been created:

  • TC1. Patron Successfully Reserves and Returns the Book by the Due Date
  • TC2. Patron Successfully Reserves but Fails to Return the Book on Time

Which of the acceptance criteria are not covered by the test cases?
options: All ACs are covered
AC4, AC7 are not covered
Only AC7 is not covered
AC6, AC9 are not covered
explanation: b) is correct. Neither of the test cases addresses AC4 or AC7. TC1 and TC2 focus on the reservation and return processes under the assumption of successful logins and interactions, without addressing the scenarios where a reservation might expire due to not being picked up or where a reservation needs to be canceled due to a failed login.

stem: Which of the following is USUALLY stated as a testing objective?
options: Start testing only when the developers deploy a stable build to the testing environment
Providing information to stakeholders to allow them to make informed decisions
To validate that there are no unexplored input combinations, as all have been tested
Prioritize defect reports and insist on including them in the next release scope
explanation: b) is correct. One of the primary objectives of testing is to deliver insights that help stakeholders understand the quality and readiness of the product, enabling them to make strategic decisions. This aligns well with the learning objective of recognizing the value of testing in the software development lifecycle.

stem:
Which characteristics (1-4) fit which test levels (A-D) BEST?

  • The main forms of testing include: user testing, operational testing, contractual and regulatory testing
  • Testing is heavily dependent on strategy approaches like bottom-up, top-down, or big-bang
  • Testing is normally performed by developers in their development environment
  • Testing may be carried out by an independent test team and is related to specifications for the system

A. Component testing

B. Component integration testing

C. System testing

D. Acceptance testing
explanation: c) is correct. It accurately matches the testing characteristics to their corresponding test levels: Acceptance testing focuses on user and regulatory tests (1D), Component integration testing relies on strategic approaches (2B), Component testing is performed by developers in their environment (3A), and System testing involves independent teams related to specifications (4C).

stem: In the context of reviews, the role of the Facilitator includes which of the following responsibilities?
options: Creating and fixing the work product under review
Ensuring the effective running of review meetings, including mediation and time management
Collating anomalies from reviewers
Deciding what is to be reviewed and providing resources
explanation: b) is correct. According to the syllabus: Moderator (also known as the facilitator) – ensures the effective running of review meetings, including mediation, time management, and a safe review environment in which everyone can speak freely.

stem:
You are testing a registration page for a web application and your task is to design test cases for the login field on the registration form. The login must be between 8 and 12 characters, alphanumeric and contain at least one capital (uppercase) letter. You want to apply the Each Choice Equivalence Partitioning test technique.

How many partitions do you need to cover?
explanation: d) is correct. The question asks about the number of partitions and not about the number of test cases. There are 7 EP to cover: 1. less than 8 characters (invalid) 2. from 8 to 12 characters (valid) 3. more than 12 characters (invalid) 4. alphanumeric (contains letters and numbers) 5. not alphanumeric (contains non-alphanumeric characters or only numbers/letters) (invalid) 6. includes capital (uppercase) letter (valid) 7. doesn't include capital (uppercase) letter (invalid) Each Choice Equivalence Partitioning test technique requires each partition at least once and you can combine the valid partitions.

stem:
Can the following information be found in the test plan?

Project: [Project Name]

Module: [Module Name]

Date: [Date]

  • Defect Information
  • Defect ID: [Auto-generated ID]
  • Severity: [High/Medium/Low]
  • Priority: [High/Medium/Low]
  • …
  • Environment
  • Operating System: [e.g., Windows 10]
  • Browser/Platform: [e.g., Chrome, iOS]
  • Version: [e.g., 2.1.0]
  • Reproduction Steps
  • [Step 1]
  • [Step 2]
  • [Step 3]
  • ...
options: Yes, the defect report can be found in the communication section
Yes, defect report templates can be found in the communication section
Yes, the defect report can be found in the documentation templates
No, the defect report can't be found in the test plan
explanation: b) is correct. Defect reporting is a crucial aspect of communication in testing processes, ensuring that templates are readily available for consistent documentation. This aligns with the learning objective of understanding the role of communication in effective testing and project management.

stem:
A new product for renting electric scooters is planned to be released next month. The testing team found a large number of bugs that were fixed. A good regression test suite has been written, from which all tests are automated. Stakeholders read reports from various departments and saw a recommendation in the test report. The test team advises to conduct acceptance testing with real potential users. Stakeholders noted that a considerable part of the budget and that they did not understand why additional testing was needed.

Which of the testing principles will MOST help the team make its case for its recommendation?
options: Tests wear out
Exhaustive testing is impossible
Absence-of-defects fallacy
Testing is context dependent
explanation: c) is correct. The absence-of-defects fallacy highlights the misconception that fixing bugs guarantees a product is error-free. This emphasizes the importance of additional testing, like acceptance testing, to ensure product quality from the user's perspective.

stem: Which of the following provides the BEST definition of the keyword "confirmation testing"?
options: Confirmation testing is a type of change-related testing focused on validating that the software system, after modifications or fixes, meets the specified requirements and is fit for release
Confirmation testing is a type of change-related testing performed after fixing a defect to confirm that a failure caused by that defect does not reoccur

Confirmation testing is a type of change-related testing that aims to confirm that the implemented changes have rectified reported defects and have not introduced any new issues, ensuring the software's readiness for deployment
Confirmation testing is a type of change-related testing to detect whether defects have been introduced or uncovered in unchanged areas of the software
explanation: b) is correct. It accurately defines confirmation testing's purpose of ensuring that previously identified defects do not persist after a fix, aligning with key learning objectives about testing processes. This reinforces the understanding of how testing ensures software quality and reliability post-defect resolution.

stem: Which of the following statements best describes static testing?
options: It is performed without executing the code
It focuses on the dynamic behavior of the software
It involves running tests on the software code
It ensures the software meets user requirements
explanation: a) is correct. In contrast to dynamic testing, in static testing the software under test does not need to be executed. Code, process specification, system architecture specification or other work products are evaluated through manual examination (e.g., reviews) or with the help of a tool (e.g., static analysis).

stem:
Consider the following state transition diagram for a login system

Assume that each test must start at the beginning state, LOGIN, and each test ends in the DASHBOARD state.

What is the MINIMAL number of test cases to achieve valid transitions coverage?
explanation: a) is correct. The minimal number of test cases required to cover all valid transitions in the state transition diagram for the login system is 3. Each test case effectively tests a unique path through the states, ensuring comprehensive validation of the login process: - TC1: Continue with Phone, Invalid code, resend SMS, Back, Continue with Phone, Valid code - TC2: Continue with Email, Invalid code, resend EMAIL, Back, Continue with Email, Valid code - TC3: Continue with Social Media, Invalid code, Back, Continue with Social Media, Valid password

stem: Which of the following BEST describes product risks in software testing?
options: Risks associated with product quality characteristics
Risks related to the management and control of the project
Risks associated with the skills and expertise of the testing team
Risks arising from supplier issues such as third-party delivery failure
explanation: a) is correct. Product quality characteristics are associated with product risks, not project risks. Product risks are related to the product quality characteristics (e.g., described in the ISO 25010 quality model). Examples of product risks include: missing or wrong functionality, incorrect calculations, runtime errors, poor architecture, inefficient algorithms, inadequate response time, poor user experience, security vulnerabilities.

stem: What is a major benefit of implementing test automation in software testing processes?
options: It eliminates the need for test planning
It guarantees the detection of every defect
It reduces the time required for repetitive testing tasks
It ensures that no manual testing is required
explanation: c) is correct. Potential benefits of using test automation include: - Time saved by reducing repetitive manual work (e.g., execute regression tests, re-enter the same test data, compare expected results vs actual results, and check against coding standards)

stem: Your team is finalizing the development of a mobile banking app, focusing now on the feature that allows users to transfer funds between accounts. Which of these activities would be classified under test implementation?
options: Designing a set of test cases to cover all possible scenarios of fund transfer
Determining the necessary sequence of test execution to cover happy and unhappy paths
Establishing a schedule for testing activities, including milestones for completing the fund transfer feature testing
Reporting bugs found during the testing of the fund transfer feature to the development team
explanation: b) is correct. Test implementation includes creating or acquiring the testware necessary for test execution (e.g., test data). Test cases can be organized into test procedures and are often assembled into test suites. Manual and automated test scripts are created. Test procedures are prioritized and arranged within a test execution schedule for efficient test execution. The test environment is built and verified to be set up correctly.

stem:
You are testing a thermostat for a heating/air conditioning system. You have been given the following requirements:

ReqNumber of units
a1(-inf; -1]
a2[0; 10]
a3[11; +inf)

The developer made a mistake in the first equivalence partition, instead of (number of units≤(-1)) developer codded (number of units=(-1))

Using boundary value analysis, which of the following sets of test inputs will identify the problem?
explanation: b) is correct. Mistake can be identified by proper use of 3-value BVA test design technique. The value (-2) will identify the issue. The following are the equivalence classes for this question: - (a1) t < 0 (-∞;-1] - (a2) 0≤ t ≤10 [0;10] - (a3) 10 < t [11; +∞) 3-value BVA: - (a1) min-1 and min are not defined, max-1: (-2), max: (-1), max+1: 0 - (a2) min-1: -1, min: 0, min+1: 1, max-1: 9, max: 10, max+1: 11 - (a3) min-1: 10, min: 11, min+1: 12, max-1, max and max+1 are not defined

stem: Which of the following is not an example of the benefits of DevOps?
options: The DevOps delivery pipeline must be defined and established
Fast feedback on the code quality, and whether changes adversely affect existing code
CI promotes a shift-left approach in testing by encouraging developers to submit high-quality code accompanied by component tests and static analysis
Promotes automated processes like CI/CD that facilitate establishing stable test environments
explanation: a) is correct. It is not a benefit of DevOps; rather, it is a prerequisite for implementing DevOps practices. Understanding this distinction highlights the importance of establishing a structured and defined workflow to fully realize the benefits of DevOps.

stem: What is the primary focus of black-box testing techniques?
options: Testing the application based on its specified behavior without reference to its internal structure
Utilizing the knowledge and experience of testers to design test cases
Analyzing the internal structure and processing of the test object
Creating test cases after the design or implementation of the code is complete
explanation: a) is correct. Black-box testing evaluates the functionality of an application solely based on its requirements and specifications, disregarding how the application is implemented internally. This approach emphasizes testing from the end-user's perspective.

stem:
Consider the following defect report:

The "Export All" feature does not work correctly in the Reporting section, and this issue surfaced after the latest release. Numerous clients have reported this problem to customer support, indicating that it is a critical issue requiring a hotfix. The system becomes unresponsive, requiring a system restart. The defect report is linked to requirement REQ-2045, which describes the "Export All" functionality, deemed essential for client data handling. Test environment and software version: Windows 10, Version 1909.

Which essential information is missing in this defect report?
options: Test environment and software version
Severity of the defect
Expected and actual results
Unique identifier and summary of the defect
explanation: c) is correct. The defect report does not explicitly state what the expected and actual results of the test were, which are necessary to clearly understand the deviation from expected behavior.

stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding the importance of communication skills for testers?
options: Testers should communicate information about defects and failures in a constructive manner, as they may be perceived as the bearers of bad news
Confirmation bias can make it difficult to accept information that disagrees with currently held beliefs, so
Testers must be capable of defending their perspectives, as developers frequently criticize them due to inadequate quality in unit tests
Testers should communicate information about defects and failures in a constructive manner, as they may face criticism as the authors of the defects in the software code
explanation: a) is correct. Effective communication helps maintain a positive relationship between testers and developers, promoting collaboration and problem-solving despite the challenges of delivering negative information. This emphasizes the importance of communication skills within the framework of testing and quality assurance.

stem: The team has recently concluded a retrospective, during which they discussed what was successful and should be retained, as well as what was not successful and could be improved. What additional factors should the team consider discussing to further identify opportunities for process enhancement?
options: How to incorporate the improvements and retain the successes in the future?
What was not successful and could be improved?
What was successful, and should be retained?
Why incorporate the improvements and retain the successes in the future?
explanation: a) is correct. It emphasizes the importance of not only identifying what worked and what didn't, but also actively planning for the integration of successful practices and enhancements in future processes. This focus on actionable steps aligns with continuous improvement principles, reinforcing effective teamwork and progression.

stem: What is the correct sequence of steps from the start of a review to its completion?
options: Review Initiation - Planning - Individual Review - Communication and Analysis - Fixing and Reporting
Planning - Review Initiation - Communication and Analysis - Individual Review - Fixing and Reporting
Planning - Review Initiation - Individual Review - Communication and Analysis - Fixing and Reporting
Planning - Review Initiation - Fixing and Reporting - Individual Review - Communication and Analysis
explanation: c) is correct. The activities in the review process are: Planning - Review Initiation - Individual Review - Communication and Analysis - Fixing and Reporting.

stem: Which of the following statements accurately describes the relationship between statement coverage and branch coverage?
options: Statement coverage focuses on executing code statements, while branch coverage focuses on testing decision outcomes
100% branch coverage automatically implies 100% statement coverage
100% statement coverage automatically implies 100% branch coverage
Statement coverage is considered a subset of branch coverage
explanation: b) is correct. Branch coverage subsumes statement coverage. This means that any set of test cases achieving 100% branch coverage also achieves 100% statement coverage (but not vice versa).

stem: Which Agile testing quadrant's tests are designed from the business perspective and may involve the use of techniques such as ATDD and BDD?
options: None
Quadrant Q2
Quadrant Q3
Quadrant Q4
explanation: b) is correct, according to the syllabus 5.1.7. Testing Quadrants. Quadrant Q1 tests should be automated and included in the CI process; Quadrant Q2 tests check the acceptance criteria and can be manual or automated; Quadrant Q3 tests are user-oriented and often manual; Quadrant Q4 tests are often automated.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical responsibility of the testing role?
options: Identifying and prioritizing test conditions and expected outcomes based on functional specifications and requirements
Identifying defects or issues encountered during test execution and documenting them in a defect tracking system
Documenting and archiving test artifacts, including test cases, results, and reports, for future reference
Verifying that test environments are properly set up before test execution
explanation: c) is correct, example of the test closure. (Note: d) is an example of test implementation, but c) is the answer as it belongs to test closure activities.)

stem: Which of the following statements about TDD is true?
options: TDD is a "test-first" approach where test cases are written in the form of unit tests and belong to quadrant two (Q2)
TDD is a "test-first" approach that includes refactoring both tests and the code written to satisfy the tests
TDD is a "test-first" approach where a test automation framework provides drafts of tests for developers, and these drafts can then be refined into executable test scripts
TDD is a "test-first" approach where tests are written by developers and then reviewed by testers and business representatives
explanation: b) is correct. TDD emphasizes the iterative cycle of creating tests before the code, as well as continuously refining both to enhance quality. This connects to the learning objective of understanding TDD's principles and methods, particularly the focus on both testing and code improvement.

stem: Which of the following is the BEST description of the error-guessing technique?
options: A structured approach to test design, focusing on input-output transformations and data flow
A method used to identify defects based on formal analysis of the software's internal logic and structure
An experience-based approach where testers use knowledge of common errors to focus their testing efforts
A testing technique primarily concerned with how end-users might incorrectly interact with the software
explanation: c) is correct. It captures the essence of the error-guessing technique, which leverages tester experience to anticipate potential defects. This aligns with learning objectives related to understanding testing methodologies that utilize historical knowledge to enhance testing efficiency and effectiveness.

stem:
Your team uses planning poker to estimate the test effort for a newly required feature.

Given the following user story: "As the registered user, I want the ability to save my preferred product filters, so that I can quickly access them for future searches"

Each estimator has a deck of cards with values similar to the Fibonacci sequence (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21)

After three rounds, the consensus was not reached. You can see the test estimation results in the table below:

Planning poker - vong 3 chua dong thuan: da so chon 5, m2 va m4 chon khac.

Which of the following is the BEST example of the next step?
options: Another round of the planning poker session should occur
Accept 5 as the final test estimate, as it has the majority of votes in the third round
m2 and m4 should explain the rationale behind their estimates, then, another round of the planning poker session should occur
Other members need to explain to m2 and m4 why they are wrong, then, another round of the planning poker session should occur
explanation: c) is correct. If all estimators selected the same value, that becomes the estimate. If not, the estimators discuss the differences in estimates after which the poker round is repeated until agreement is reached by consensus, as no rules are defined by the team.

stem: Which of the following is an advantage of the whole team approach?
options: It enhances collaboration within the team by using the Agile board, making it visible which team members are taking an unsatisfactory amount of time to complete their tasks
It improves team dynamics, enhances communication, and collaboration within the team
It makes quality everyone's responsibility, as the whole team is a part of the test design activity and requires training in test design techniques
It makes quality everyone's responsibility by clearly defining the limits of each team member's responsibilities
explanation: b) is correct. A whole team approach fosters a culture of open dialogue and shared responsibility, which ultimately leads to more effective teamwork and project outcomes. This aligns with the learning objective of understanding how team collaboration impacts overall performance in Agile methodologies.

stem: Which of the following is the BEST description of exploratory testing?
options: A formal test technique used to design test cases from a specification
A structured approach requiring detailed test design before execution
An informal approach where design, execution, and learning occur simultaneously
An approach solely focused on the external interfaces of the system or component
explanation: c) is correct. In exploratory testing, tests are simultaneously designed, executed, and evaluated while the tester learns about the test object. The testing is used to learn more about the test object, to explore it more deeply with focused tests, and to create tests for untested areas.

stem:
During an iteration planning meeting, the team is sharing their thoughts about the following acceptance criteria of the user story:

Title: Enhance User Experience with Improved Page Performance

  • As a frequent user of the platform,
  • I want the home page and login/register pages to load faster and provide a smoother experience,
  • So that I can quickly access and navigate through the site without unnecessary delays or interruptions.

Priority: High

Story points: 5

  • The home page and login/register pages should load noticeably faster compared to the previous version, providing a smoother user experience.
  • Users should experience a perceptible reduction in wait time during page loading across different network speeds.

Which of the following would best represent a tester's contribution to this discussion?
options: The tester advises that the story should be divided into two separate user stories for each page
The tester advises that the security of the home page and login/register pages should be improved
The tester suggests increasing the priority and estimation of the user story
The tester advises that the user story needs acceptance criteria to be testable
explanation: d) is correct. The tester contributes by ensuring that the team creates testable acceptance criteria for the user story. "Load noticeably faster" and "perceptible reduction in wait time" are subjective acceptance criteria, and need to be measurable.

stem: Which of the following is the BEST describes the sequential development models?
options: Testing is typically delayed in the SDLC until the later phases when executable code is generated
Static testing is frequently omitted or bypassed, while dynamic testing cannot be performed early in the SDLC and is typically conducted in later stages
Both static and dynamic testing are typically performed at all stages of the SDLC
Dynamic testing is typically conducted in the later stages of the SDLC, while static testing is performed in the early stages
explanation: d) is correct. Static testing, which includes reviews and inspections, helps catch issues early in the development process, while dynamic testing relies on executable code and is therefore conducted after some functionality is built. This distinction is essential for understanding the flow of testing within the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).

stem: What is the primary benefit of white-box testing when dealing with vague or incomplete software specifications?
options: It enables testers to identify defects based on the internal workings of the software
It confirms that the user interface meets user expectations
It ensures that the system's performance meets the benchmark criteria
It guarantees that all user requirements are correctly implemented
explanation: a) is correct. White-box testing allows testers to focus on the internal structure and logic of the code, which is especially valuable when specifications are vague or incomplete. This approach enhances defect detection by revealing issues that may not be apparent through just examining external outputs.

stem:
You are testing an online platform that connects people who want to rent their homes or accommodations with travelers seeking temporary lodging. The platform allows hosts to list their properties, which can range from entire homes and apartments to individual rooms, and travelers can book these accommodations for short-term stays. You need to execute test cases in accordance with the specified execution schedule. Test cases are organized into two test suites, retesting and regression. The retesting test suite should be tested first, the regression test suite immediately after it. Consider the following list of test cases, test suites, priorities and coverages:

TC IDReqPriorityCoverageTS
TC1Superhost StatusMedium15%Regression
TC2Multi-language SupportLow10%Retesting
TC3Wish ListV.Low10%Retesting
TC4Search & BookHigh25%Regression
TC5Property ListingsHigh20%Regression
TC6Booking CalendarHigh25%Retesting
TC7Host ProfilesMedium20%Regression
TC8Messaging SystemHigh15%Retesting

You aim to prioritize test cases using coverage-based prioritization, wherein the test execution sequence is determined by the coverage of the single test case. In case the coverage percentage achieved by test cases is the same, the test case with the highest severity is executed first.

Given this information, what is the proper order in which to execute these test cases?
options: TC6 - TC8 - TC2 - TC3 - TC4 - TC5 - TC7 - TC1
TC6 - TC4 - TC5 - TC8 - TC7 - TC1 - TC3 - TC2
TC4 - TC6 - TC5 - TC8 - TC7 - TC1 - TC3 - TC2
TC4 - TC5 - TC7 - TC1 - TC6 - TC8 - TC2 - TC3
explanation: a) is correct. It follows the recommended order of executing test cases based on coverage and severity: - Prioritization criteria: Test cases are executed based on coverage to ensure critical functionality is tested first, and severity to focus on issues that could have the most impact. - Order based on coverage: High coverage test cases should be executed earlier to maximize the chances of catching defects early in the testing cycle. - Order based on severity: Among tests with similar coverage, those with higher severity (critical issues) are typically prioritized to address the most impactful defects sooner. - Sequence in answer a): It starts with TC6 and TC8, which likely have the highest coverage and severity, then proceeds through other tests, respecting the importance of testing those features first and detecting high-impact defects early on. - Retesting and regression considerations: The sequence respects the logical flow—retesting critical areas first before moving to regression tests—supporting effective defect detection and efficient testing.

stem: What is the primary purpose of using test management tools in software testing?
options: To automate all testing activities and eliminate the need for manual testing
To facilitate the process of compiling and executing code
To manage test cases, plans, and reports, and to track defects
To enhance the performance of applications under test
explanation: c) is correct. Management tools – increase the test process efficiency by facilitating management of the SDLC, requirements, tests, defects, configuration.

stem:
Project: Online Shopping Website

Version: v2.0

Planned Testing Window: 2023-08-15 to 2023-08-30

Test Environment:

  • Test Environment Name: TestingEnvironment_v2
  • Hardware: Intel Core i7, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD
  • Software: Windows 10, Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox
  • Network Configuration: Local Area Network

Test Execution Phases:

  • Phase 1 (Smoke Testing): Scheduled for 2023-08-15 – 2023-08-17
  • Phase 2 (Functional Testing): Scheduled for 2023-08-18 – 2023-08-22
  • Phase 3 (Regression Testing): Scheduled for 2023-08-23 – 2023-08-25

Which test activity produces this testware as an output?
options: Test implementation
Test design
Test execution
Test analysis
explanation: a) is correct. Test implementation includes creating the test execution schedule. The provided artifact contains a timeline for when tests are scheduled to occur (test execution schedule), which is a work product of test implementation.

stem:
A company's employees are eligible for bonuses if they have worked at the company for more than a year and have achieved an individually agreed-upon target.

These conditions can be represented in a decision table:

R1R2R3R4R5R6R7R8
Worked>1yrYYYYNNNN
Agreed targetYYNNYYNN
Achieved targetYNYNYNYN
BonusYNYNNNNN

Based on the table of the bonus system, which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: R1, R2, can't be merged into a single column
R3 describes an impossible situation
R2 describes an impossible situation
R2, R4, R6, R8 can be merged into a single column
explanation: c) is correct. The statement is FALSE: In R2, the employee agreed on a target (YES) but didn't achieve the target (NO) and therefore didn't get the bonus (NO). This is a logical and possible scenario, as the bonus is only granted when the target is both agreed upon and achieved. (Note: b) is TRUE - In R3, the employee didn't agree on a target (NO) but achieved the target (YES). However, the system still indicates a bonus payment (YES). This situation is impossible, as bonuses cannot be granted if no target was agreed upon, regardless of whether the target was achieved.)

stem: What should a typical Test Progress Report include?
options: Test summary and product quality evaluation
New and changed risks within the testing period
Unmitigated risks and defects not fixed
Lessons learned that are relevant to the testing
explanation: b) is correct. A Test Progress Report focuses on current challenges and risks which are essential for ongoing test activities.

stem:
Consider the following user story:

• As a library patron, I want to be able to reserve a book online, so that I can pick it up at my convenience

And its acceptance criteria:

  • The patron can search for books by title, author, or keyword
  • The patron can see if a book is available for reservation
  • The patron must be logged in to their library account to place a reservation
  • Reservations expire after 3 days if not picked up
  • When a patron arrives to pick up a reserved book, they must log in to the library system to confirm their identity
  • If login is successful, the librarian can locate the reservation and mark the book as "unavailable"
  • If login is unsuccessful, the reservation is canceled
  • The checkout period for a book is 21 days
  • If a book is returned on or before its due date, the librarian marks it as "available" in the system

Which of the following is BEST example of a test case would logically be the first to be created and run?
options: A patron, searches for a book, finds it "available", logs in, places a reservation, comes to pick up the book, but cannot log in to the system, the reservation is canceled

A patron logs in, searches for a book, places a reservation, successfully pick ups a reserved book on the fifth day of reservation, a librarian marks the book as "unavailable", and a patron returns it in two weeks
A patron, searches for a book, finds it "available", logs in, places a reservation, successfully pick ups a reserved book on the second day of reservation, and returns it within one week

A patron searches for a book, places a reservation, and successfully pick ups a reserved book on the first day of reservation, marks the book as "unavailable", returns it within two weeks, and marks the book as "available"
explanation: c) is correct. Typically, the first test cases are positive, confirming the correct behavior without exceptions or error conditions, and comprising the sequence of activities executed if everything goes as expected.

stem: Which of the following work products are examinable by static testing?
options: Only source code
Only test cases
Any tangible work product including code, specifications, designs, and documents
Only test plans
explanation: c) is correct. Almost any work product can be examined using static testing. Examples include requirement specification documents, source code, test plans, test cases, product backlog items, test charters, project documentation, contracts and models. Any work product that can be read and understood can be the subject of a review. However, for static analysis, work products need a structure against which they can be checked (e.g., models, code or text with a formal syntax).

stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the difference between testing and debugging?
options: Dynamic testing triggers failures that are caused by defects; debugging checks whether the fixes resolved the problem
Static testing triggers failures that are caused by defects; debugging finds causes of defects and fixes them
Static testing directly finds defects in the test object; debugging finds causes of defects and fixes them
Dynamic testing directly finds defects in the test object; debugging finds causes of defects and fixes them
explanation: c) is correct. Static testing finds defects directly in the test object (like code or documents), and debugging involves identifying and fixing the causes of defects.

stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY benefit of collaborative user story writing in an agile development environment?
options: It promotes a shared understanding of requirements across different team roles
It ensures that user stories conform strictly to the INVEST principles
It eliminates the need for later reviews or changes to user stories
It guarantees that all potential defects will be identified early in the process
explanation: a) is correct. While other options touch on potential outcomes, the main advantage of collaboration is ensuring everyone involved (business, development, testing) has the same understanding of what's being built and why.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a primary goal of configuration management (CM) in testing?
options: Uniquely identifying all configuration items
Controlling changes to configuration items through a formal process
Tracking changes to configuration items
Automating test execution
explanation: d) is correct. While CM can be integrated with automation tools, its focus is on managing the configuration items, not executing the tests themselves.

stem: In what way can test results be used in testing?
options: Test results are used to guarantee that no defects remain in the software
Test results can be used to fix defects
Test results can be used to provide feedback on how well the test processes are performing
It measures the quality of software in terms of number of executed test cases
explanation: b) Is correct. Per syllabus. Test results are used by QA and testing. In testing they are used to fix defects, while in QA they provide feedback on how well the development and test processes are performing.

stem: Which of the following is a good testing practice that applies to all software development lifecycles?
options: It's imperative that all tests are automated and included in the continuous integration process whenever there is a software change
When it comes to sharing information with and within a development team, face-to-face conversation is the most efficient and effective method
As soon as coding is finished, and all system components are available for testing, test analysis and design for any test levels should begin
It is essential for every test level to establish its own set of test objectives that are coherent with the phase or activities targeted within the software development lifecycle
explanation: d) is correct. Every test level should have its own test objectives that are coherent with the phase or activities targeted within the SDLC. This is a good testing practice that applies to all software development lifecycles.

stem: What practice facilitates obtaining frequent stakeholder feedback?
options: Waterfall development approach
Sprint reviews or demos
Annual project reviews
Limited stakeholder involvement
explanation: b) is correct. Agile projects use short iterations during the development cycle. Within these short cycles, feature clarification, design, code and test takes place. At the end of the cycle, the team have produced a 'minimum viable product' (MVP). The MVP contains a very limited subset of proposed system features, but is sufficient to enable meaningful feedback to be gathered from the product's initial users. Each subsequent development iteration then adds to the product until, eventually, the entire system is complete. Business representatives on the project assist in feature prioritisation, resulting in frequent stakeholder feedback.

stem:
You want to apply branch testing to the code represented by the following control flow graph.

How many coverage items do you need to test?
explanation: d) is correct. In branch testing the coverage items are branches. A branch is a transfer of control between two nodes in the control flow graph, which shows the possible sequences in which source code statements are executed in the test object. Each transfer of control can be either unconditional (i.e., straight-line code) or conditional (i.e., a decision outcome).

stem:
Your team uses planning poker to estimate the test effort for a newly required feature.

Given the following user story: "As a user, I want to be able to easily upload and manage images on the platform so that I can seamlessly share my visual content with others"

Each estimator has a deck of cards with values similar to the shirt sizes ranging from extra-small to extra-extra-large (XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL)

During the first poker planning session, the following story points were given based on risk, effort, complexity, and proper extent of testing:

Team members estimation:

  • Customers: M
  • Developers: M
  • Testers: XXL

What is the best outcome following this planning session?
options: Because the customer's and developer's size estimates match, the team can be confident that this estimate is good and should move to the next user story
The team should hold a conversation to understand why the testers felt this user story was significantly more work. Another round of the planning poker session should occur following that discussion
Because the customer owns the system in the end, the customers' estimates should be taken as correct when there is a conflict
The poker planning sessions should continue until all estimated story sizes are an exact match between developers and testers
explanation: b) Is correct. Planning poker sessions should continue for the user story until the entire team is satisfied with the estimated effort.

stem: Which of the following is NOT considered a contextual factor affecting testing activities?
options: The personal preferences of the test team members regarding coding languages
Stakeholders' business needs
Industry standards
Software development methodologies
explanation: a) is correct. The way the testing is carried out will depend on a number of contextual factors including: - Software development lifecycle (engineering practices, development methods, etc.) - Stakeholders (needs, expectations, requirements, willingness to cooperate, etc.) - Business domain (criticality of the test object, identified risks, market needs, specific legal regulations, etc.)

stem:
A smart home app measures the average temperature in the house over the previous week and provides feedback to the occupants on their environmental friendliness based on this temperature.

The feedback for different average temperature ranges (to the nearest °C) should be:

  • Below 0°C - Let It Go! Let It Go!
  • Up to 10°C - Icy Cool!
  • 11°C to 16°C - Chilled Out!
  • 17°C to 18°C - Cool Man!
  • 19°C to 23°C - Too Warm!
  • Above 23°C - Hot & Sweaty!

You have prepared the following set of test cases:

  • TC1 (-10°C) - Let It Go! Let It Go!
  • TC2 (-1°C) - Let It Go! Let It Go!
  • TC3 9°C - Icy Cool!
  • TC4 16°C - Chilled Out!
  • TC5 17°C - Cool Man!
  • TC6 18°C - Cool Man!
  • TC7 22°C - Too Warm!
  • TC8 23°C - Hot & Sweaty!

What is the 2-value Boundary Value Analysis (BVA) coverage for the final result that is achieved with the existing test cases?
explanation: b) is correct. For the input equivalence partitions given, the above used boundary value technique yields the following coverage items: -1, 0, 10, 11, 16, 17, 18, 19, 23, 24 (10 items). The test cases cover 5 of them (-1, 16, 17, 18, 23), which gives 50% coverage.

stem: Which of the following statements about 'Configuration Management' is FALSE?
options: Configuration Management negates the necessity for continuous integration and continuous deployment in DevOps
Configuration Management helps in maintaining traceability throughout the test process by relating and tracking changes in configuration items
Configuration Management facilitates the reproduction of previous test results by allowing reversion to previous baselines
All configuration items in Configuration Management are uniquely identified and version-controlled
explanation: a) is correct. Configuration Management does not negate the necessity for continuous integration or deployment; rather, it is typically part of an automated DevOps pipeline that includes these processes, ensuring consistent and reliable handling of configuration items.

stem: Which of the following statements about BDD is true?
options: BDD involves collaboration among developers, testers, and customers to define acceptance criteria before development begins
BDD tests belong to quadrant four (Q4) and help developers understand non-functional system characteristics like performance, security, portability, and maintainability
In BDD, acceptance criteria are typically created based on the given/when/then format and then automatically translated into executable tests
In BDD, tests are created based on acceptance criteria to drive the development of the related software
explanation: c) is correct. According to the syllabus, BDD expresses the desired behavior of an application with test cases written in a simple form of natural language, which is easy to understand by stakeholders – usually using the Given/When/Then format. Test cases are then automatically translated into executable tests.

stem: Which of the following best describes Exploratory Testing?
options: A rigorous and formalized testing process where test cases are planned in advance and executed in a strict order
A testing technique where the software is explored in real-time, with tests being designed and executed simultaneously based on the tester's current understanding
A type of testing where all possible errors are guessed in advance and tests are designed to detect these specific errors
Testing that is exclusively performed by automated testing tools to explore all possible paths through the software
explanation: b) is correct. In exploratory testing, tests are simultaneously designed, executed, and evaluated while the tester learns about the test object. The testing is used to learn more about the test object, to explore it more deeply with focused tests, and to create tests for untested areas.

stem: How is the whole team approach present in the interactions between testers and developers?
options: Developers write unit tests while testers create system test cases
Developers create unit tests, then testers review and fix those
Testers work closely with developers on test automation approaches
Developers are responsible for the code quality, while testers are responsible for product quality
explanation: c) is correct. In the whole team approach, testers work closely with developers on test automation approaches, leveraging the various skill sets within the team for the benefit of the project.

stem:
You are testing a mobile app that allows users to find a nearby restaurant, based on the type of food they want to eat. Consider the following list of test cases, priorities (smaller number is high priority), and dependencies, in the following format:

TC IDPriorityDependencies
01.0011—
01.0022—
01.0033—
01.004501.003
01.0054—

Which of the following is a possible test execution schedule that considers both priorities and dependencies?
explanation: b) is correct. This schedule considers both priorities and dependencies: test cases are executed in priority order, and each test case is only executed after its dependencies have been satisfied. 01.004 depends on 01.003, so it is executed after 01.003 and 01.005 (which has a higher priority than 01.004).

stem:
Consider the following state transition diagram for the e-banking system.

Assume further that each test must start at the S1 state, login, and each test ends when a transition arrives back at the S1, login, state.

Which of the following test cases, represented as sequences of events, covers ONLY valid transitions?
options: restart → valid credentials → check balance → back → withdraw → valid amount
valid credentials → withdraw → invalid amount → back → check balance → back → back → cancel
valid credentials → withdraw → invalid amount → back → check balance → withdraw → valid amount
valid credentials → check balance → withdraw → invalid amount → check balance → withdraw → valid amount
explanation: c) is correct. Contains only valid transitions. - a) is not correct. After the transition 'restart', we are back to the state S1 (Login). The test must end when a transition arrives back at S1, so the test case shouldn't continue after the first transition. - b) is not correct. There is no valid 'back' transition from S2.

stem: Which of the following statements best describes a key difference between static testing and dynamic testing?
options: Static testing involves executing the software code, while dynamic testing focuses on reviewing documents and code without executing the program
Dynamic testing involves reviewing the code and documents without executing the software, while static testing focuses on executing the program to uncover defects
Both static and dynamic testing involve executing the software code, but dynamic testing focuses on uncovering defects through code review, while static testing involves executing test cases
Static testing focuses on analyzing code and documents without executing the software, while dynamic testing involves executing the program to identify defects through actual execution
explanation: d) is correct. In contrast to dynamic testing, in static testing the software under test does not need to be executed. Code, process specification, system architecture specification or other work products are evaluated through manual examination (e.g., reviews) or with the help of a tool (e.g., static analysis).

stem: Implementing test automation may introduce a dependency on the tool vendor. How can this risk be mitigated?
options: Avoid open-source tools at all costs
Select a vendor with a strong reputation and track record
Only use tools developed in-house
It's impossible to completely mitigate vendor-related risks
explanation: b) is correct. Potential risks of using test automation include: - The dependency on the tool vendor which may go out of business, retire the tool, sell the tool to a different vendor or provide poor support (e.g., responses to queries, upgrades, and defect fixes). - Using an open-source software which may be abandoned, meaning that no further updates are available, or its internal components may require quite frequent updates as a further development. Selecting a vendor with a strong reputation and track record mitigates the risk of vendor dependency.

stem: How does white-box testing enhance the effectiveness of test cases designed for black-box testing?
options: By ensuring that all user interfaces are thoroughly tested
By identifying areas of the code not exercised by black-box test cases, thus highlighting additional test needs
By reducing the overall number of test cases needed to achieve full acceptance criteria coverage
By focusing exclusively on performance and load testing scenarios
explanation: b) is correct. White-box testing can enhance the effectiveness of black-box test cases by identifying areas of the code not exercised by those test cases, thus highlighting additional test needs.

stem: Which of the following BEST explains a drawback of independent testing?
options: Despite the fact that independent testers have different backgrounds, technical perspectives, and biases from developers, they mostly find the same kind of defects
Independent testers may feel they are not part of the development team
An independent testing team may be more focused on learning how the software works than focusing on detecting defects
After some time, the independent testing team learns a lot about the system, which reduces the quality and efficiency of testing
explanation: b) is correct. A drawback of independent testing is that independent testers may feel they are not part of the development team, which can lead to a lack of collaboration and communication problems.

stem:
Given the following examples of entry and exit criteria:

  • The test cases have achieved a 90% statement coverage
  • The integration system test suite achieved a 100% success rate as all smoke test cases passed
  • Ensuring a defect density below 1% guarantees a satisfactory level of quality for deployment
  • The subscription for the UI testing tool has been purchased, and access has been granted to all members of the testing team
  • Sample data, similar to that in the production environment, has been added to the test environment database
  • All critical defects are addressed and fixed to ensure a robust and reliable software release

Which of the following BEST categorizes them as entry and exit criteria:
options: Entry criteria – 2, 4, 5; Exit criteria – 1, 3, 6
Entry criteria – 4, 5; Exit criteria – 1, 2, 3, 6
Entry criteria – 1, 4, 6; Exit criteria – 2, 3, 5
Entry criteria – 2, 3, 5; Exit criteria – 1, 4, 6
explanation: a) is correct. - 2. All smoke test cases passed with a 100% success rate - example of the need for a test object to have met the exit criteria for a prior level of testing before testing can begin (entry criterion) - 4. The subscription for the UI testing tool has been purchased, and access granted - entry criterion (availability of test tools) - 5. Sample data added to the test environment database - entry criterion (test environment readiness) - 1. 90% statement coverage achieved - exit criterion - 3. Defect density below 1% - exit criterion - 6. All critical defects addressed and fixed - exit criterion

stem:
A fitness app measures the number of steps that are walked each day and provides feedback to encourage the user to keep fit.

The feedback for different numbers of steps should be:

  • Up to 1000 - Couch Potato!
  • Above 1000, up to 4000 - Getting There!
  • Above 4000, up to 6000 - Not Bad!
  • Above 6000 up to 9999 - Way to Go!
  • Above 9999 - Champion!

Which of the following sets of test inputs would achieve the BEST equivalence partition coverage?
explanation: c) Is correct. 1 (1), 1000 (1), 4000 (2), 5000 (3), 10000 (5) – 4 partitions (out of 5). This option provides the best equivalence partition coverage among the given options.

stem: Which of the following statements about retrospectives is true?
options: A retrospective is an internal technical meeting that takes place at the end of an iteration, where testers and developers discuss how to improve communication, code coverage, and the sequence of deployments
The main focus of the retrospective is the discussion of problems that arose during the iteration, the manager should write them down and address them

In Agile development, there are many meetings: daily stand-up, release planning, iteration planning, etc. With the help of a retrospective, you can determine which of the meetings are optional and eliminate those

Retrospectives are an effective way to determine which project processes can be improved. In addition, meeting participants should take into account the project's limitations and accordingly determine how these processes can be implemented
explanation: d) is correct. Retrospectives are an effective way to determine which project processes can be improved, taking into account the project's limitations and determining how these processes can be implemented.

stem:
Consider the following characteristics (1-4) and agile testing quadrants (A-D):

  • This quadrant contains functional tests, examples, user story tests, user experience prototypes, API testing, and simulations
  • This quadrant contains smoke tests and non-functional tests
  • This quadrant contains component and component integration tests
  • This quadrant contains exploratory testing, usability testing, user acceptance testing
  • A. Agile testing quadrant Q1: technology facing, supporting the development team
  • B. Agile testing quadrant Q2: business facing, supporting the development team
  • C. Agile testing quadrant Q3: business facing, critique the product
  • D. Agile testing quadrant Q4: technology facing, critique the product

How do the following test categories map onto the agile testing quadrants?
explanation: c) is correct, according to the syllabus 5.1.7. Testing Quadrants. Quadrant Q1 contains component and component integration tests; Quadrant Q2 contains functional tests, examples, user story tests, user experience prototypes, API testing, and simulations; Quadrant Q3 contains exploratory testing, usability testing, user acceptance testing; Quadrant Q4 contains smoke tests and non-functional tests (except usability tests).

stem: Which of the following practices is likely to hinder a successful review?
options: Participants should dedicate adequate time to the review
Splitting large work products into smaller parts to make the required effort less intense
Participants should focus entirely on finding the author's mistakes
Failures found should be acknowledged, appreciated, and handled objectively
explanation: c) is correct. To ensure successful reviews, it's important to clearly define objectives and measurable exit criteria, without evaluating participants. Reviews should focus on the work product, not on the author. Focusing on finding the author's mistakes creates an unsafe review environment and hinders a successful review.

stem:
Your favorite bicycle daily rental store has just introduced a new Customer Relationship Management system and asked you, one of their most loyal members, to test it.

The implemented features are as follows:

  • Anyone can rent a bicycle, but members receive a 20% discount
  • However, if the return deadline is missed, the discount is no longer available
  • After 10 rentals, members get a gift: a T-shirt
  • After 10 rentals, not a member gets a gift: One free rental

How many test cases are needed to achieve 100% decision design coverage if the full decision has enough columns to cover every combination of conditions?
explanation: b) is correct. There are three conditions: - Being a member: (T/F) - Missed deadline: (T/F) - 10th rental: (T/F) Possible combinations: TTT, TTF, TFT, TFF, FTT, FTF, FFT, FFF – 8 combinations, so 8 test cases are needed for 100% decision table coverage.

stem:
After the release of a recent software update, the customer support team receives a ticket reporting an issue related to the submission of the "Your Address" form. According to the customer, when they attempt to submit the form, an error message is displayed, preventing successful submission. After a thorough examination, it was discovered that the issue lies in outdated JavaScript code on the Contact Us page.

Which of the following statements is true?
options: The failing form submission is a defect, the outdated JavaScript code is the root cause
The failing form submission is an error, the outdated JavaScript code is a defect
The failing form submission is a failure, the outdated JavaScript code is a fault
The failing form submission is a failure, the outdated JavaScript code is a root cause
explanation: c) is correct. A failure is an event in which the system does not perform a required function within the specified limits – the failing form submission observed by the customer is a failure. The defect (fault) is the flaw in the code – the outdated JavaScript code. The root cause is the earliest action or condition that contributed to the failure.

stem:
Consider the following user story:

• As a frequent traveler, I want to receive notifications about flight delays, cancellations, or gate changes via my preferred method (email or SMS), so I can adjust my plans accordingly

And its acceptance criteria:

  • The user can subscribe to flight notifications by entering their flight number, date, and preferred notification method (email or SMS)
  • The user must provide a valid email address (if email is selected) or a valid mobile phone number (if SMS is selected)
  • The user should select the timeframe in which they want to receive notifications (48 hours before departure or 24 hours before departure)
  • The system will send a notification to the user's chosen method if the flight status changes to "delayed" or canceled
  • The user can change their preferred notification method at any time by repeating steps 1-3
  • The user can unsubscribe from notifications immediately after initial subscribing or after changing their notification method

The development team has completed an initial round of testing. They have verified the following:

• User subscribes for 48-hour email notifications, receives a delayed flight notification, changes to 24-hour phone notifications, receives another delayed notification, unsubscribes, and verifies they no longer receive flight notifications

Which of the following acceptance criteria likely has NOT been fully tested in this cycle?
options: All ACs are covered
