AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6 are not covered
Only AC4 is not covered
AC4, AC6 are not covered
explanation: d) is correct. - AC1: Covered as the user subscribes with both email and SMS - AC2: Covered since valid email and valid phone number implied by successful notifications - AC3: Covered as both timeframes (48 hours and 24 hours) were used - AC4: Partially covered. The test involved notifications for "delay", but did not cover notifications for "cancel" - AC5: Covered as the user changed their notification method from email to SMS - AC6: Partially covered. The test verified the ability to unsubscribe after changing notification methods, but did not test unsubscribing immediately after the initial subscription

stem: Which type of testing technique is most appropriate for validating that an e-commerce application gives a discount only when the total purchase exceeds a certain amount?
options: Structure-based testing because it requires detailed knowledge of how discounts are calculated internally
Black-box testing because it focuses on whether the application behaves as expected according to the requirements, regardless of how the functionality is implemented
Experience-based testing, as it relies on the tester's personal intuition and experience with shopping applications
Risk-based testing, which prioritizes tests based on the potential impact of defects in the discount functionality
explanation: b) is correct. Black-box testing (also known as specification-based testing) is based on an analysis of the specified behavior of the test object without reference to its internal structure. Validating that a discount is given only when the total purchase exceeds a certain amount is about checking the application's behavior against the requirements.

stem:
You work on a fitness tracking app for a personal training company.

Your task is: "To check the functional completeness, functional correctness, and functional appropriateness"

What levels of testing are you MOST LIKELY performing?

  • i. Component testing
  • ii. Component integration testing
  • iii. System testing
  • iv. System integration testing
  • v. Acceptance testing
options: iv, v
iii, iv, v
ii, iii, iv, v
i, ii, iii, iv, v
explanation: d) is correct. All the four test types (Functional testing, Non-functional testing, Black-box testing, White-box testing) can be applied to all test levels, although the focus will be different at each level. Different test techniques can be used to derive test conditions and test cases for all the mentioned test types.

stem: What is the primary purpose of defining acceptance criteria for a user story?
options: To determine the programming language to be used for development
To establish a baseline for what must be met for the story to be accepted
To document the project budget constraints
To concentrate on positive scenarios of users' behavior
explanation: b) is correct. Acceptance criteria are used to: - Define the scope of the user story - Reach consensus among the stakeholders - Describe both positive and negative scenarios - Serve as a basis for the user story acceptance testing - Allow accurate planning and estimation

stem: Identify the statement that does NOT appropriately represent the advantages of traceability between the test basis and test work products:
options: Traceability between the test basis and testware allows the determination of which requirements are covered by test cases
Traceability between the test basis and testware is most effective when using experience-based techniques
Traceability between the test basis and testware allows the evaluation of the level of residual risk in a test object
Traceability between the test basis and testware supports coverage evaluation, making it very useful if measurable coverage criteria are defined in the test basis
explanation: b) is correct (i.e., this statement does NOT represent an advantage of traceability). Traceability is most closely related to black-box test techniques where coverage items can be derived from the test basis. Experience-based techniques do not derive coverage items from the test basis, so traceability is not most effective with them.

stem: What is the primary goal of product risk analysis in software testing?
options: To ensure that every possible defect is identified and fixed before release
To provide an awareness of product risk in order to focus testing efforts effectively
To completely eliminate all risks associated with a product
To document all possible risks for compliance purposes
explanation: b) is correct. According to the syllabus: From a testing perspective, the goal of product risk analysis is to provide an awareness of product risk in order to focus the testing effort in a way that minimizes the residual level of product risk. Ideally, product risk analysis begins early in the SDLC.

stem: Non-functional testing tools are particularly useful because they:
options: Help in managing the software development lifecycle (SDLC)
Support automated test execution and coverage measurement
Allow the tester to perform testing that is difficult or impossible to perform manually
Facilitate the generation of test cases and test data
explanation: c) is correct. According to the syllabus: Non-functional testing tools – allow the tester to perform non-functional testing that is difficult or impossible to perform manually.

stem:
Which of the following should be included in a defect report created during dynamic testing?

  • i. Unique identifier for the defect
  • ii. Test schedule
  • iii. Documented lessons learned from previous projects
  • iv. Identification of the test object and test environment
  • v. Contact information of the technical lead
  • vi. Status of the defect
options: i, iv, vi
i, iii, iv, vi
i, iv, v, vi
i, ii, iv, vi
explanation: a) is correct. According to the syllabus: A defect report typically includes: - Unique identifier - Title with a short summary - Date when the anomaly was observed, issuing organization, and author, including their role - Identification of the test object and test environment - Context of the defect - Description of the failure, the steps that detected the anomaly, and any relevant test logs, database dumps, screenshots, or recordings - Expected results and actual results - Severity - Priority - Status - References

stem: Which of the following is an example of addressing one of the testing principles?
options: Tests wear out, so you need to automate regression test suites
Exhaustive testing is impossible, therefore, testing should be limited in time, and testers should try to fit into it
Due to the Absence-of-defects fallacy testing principle, the lower the level of test independence, the more bugs testers will find
Testing is context-dependent, so test practices that have been applied successfully on one project may work poorly or not at all on another
explanation: d) is correct. This directly reflects the "testing is context dependent" testing principle. Testing is done differently in different contexts. For example, safety-critical software is tested differently from an e-commerce application.

stem: Which statement regarding the shift-left approach is correct?
options: The shift-left approach can be achieved only with test automation and tools
The shift-left approach integrates manual testing practices like static analysis alongside test automation and tools
The shift-left approach emphasizes early testing automation, primarily involving testers in TDD, unit testing, and component integration testing
The shift-left approach heavily relies on both manual testing methods like reviews and automated testing practices such as TDD
explanation: d) Is correct. This statement is correct because the syllabus explicitly mentions both manual activities like reviewing specifications and automated practices like TDD as part of a shift-left strategy.

stem: Which of the following is the MOST important consideration when designing a checklist for testing?
options: It should contain items that can be easily automated
It should reflect common software failure patterns
It should be as long and detailed as possible
It should primarily focus on achieving 100% requirements coverage
explanation: b) is correct. Certified Tester Foundation Level Syllabus, 4.4.3. Checklist-Based Testing. Checklists can be built based on experience, knowledge about what is important for the user, or an understanding of why and how software fails.

stem: Which of the following review types is the MOST formal and adheres to a strictly defined process?
options: Walkthrough
Informal Review
Technical Review
Inspection
explanation: d) is correct. As inspections are the most formal type of review, they follow the complete generic process. The main objective is to find the maximum number of anomalies. Other objectives are to evaluate quality, build confidence in the work product, and to motivate and enable authors to improve. Metrics are collected and used to improve the SDLC, including the inspection process. In inspections, the author cannot act as the review leader or scribe.

stem: In the 'Test planning' activity, what testware is produced as the output?
options: Test plan, test schedule, risk register, test charters, entry and exit criteria
Test plan, test schedule, risk register, entry and exit criteria
Test plan, test schedule, risk register, test procedures, entry and exit criteria
Test plan, test schedule, risk register, test data requirements, test environment requirements, entry and exit criteria
explanation: b) is correct. In the test planning activity, the outputs (testware) are the test plan(s), test schedule, risk register, and entry and exit criteria.

stem: Which of the following is true regarding the test pyramid?
options: The pyramid layers represent groups of tests, with the single test coverage decreasing and the execution time increasing as the layer goes lower
The pyramid layers represent groups of tests, with the single test coverage increasing and the execution time decreasing as the layer goes higher
The pyramid layers represent groups of tests, with both the single test coverage and execution time increasing as the layer goes lower
The pyramid layers represent groups of tests, with both the single test coverage and execution time decreasing as the layer goes lower
explanation: d) is correct. In the test pyramid, going lower in the pyramid (towards unit tests), each single test covers less functionality and executes faster. Going higher (towards end-to-end/UI tests), each single test covers more functionality and takes longer to execute.

stem:
You are a tester of a mobile fitness application. A new version of the operating system for smartphones is expected to be released next month. After reading the documentation, the development team states that your application does not need to be updated and should work on the new operating system as it currently does. You should propose a testing strategy.

Which of the following about maintenance testing is MOST likely true?
options: Regression testing is not required in the scope of maintenance testing
Confirmation testing is required in the scope of maintenance testing
Regression testing is required in the scope of maintenance testing
Maintainability and reliability testing are required in the scope of maintenance testing
explanation: c) is correct. Since the application is not modified (no changes to the application itself), confirmation testing is not needed. However, the environment is changing (new OS version), so regression testing is required to verify that the application still works correctly in the new environment. This is a case of maintenance testing triggered by an environment change.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical means of communicating test status to stakeholders?
options: Verbal communication during team meetings
Dashboards displaying test progress
Test data and test environment elements
Formal test reports summarizing test activities
explanation: c) is correct. While these are crucial for the testing process itself, they are not the primary means of communicating the status of testing to stakeholders. Stakeholders typically need summaries and insights, not the raw data or environment details. Typical means of communicating test status include verbal communication during team meetings, dashboards displaying test progress, and formal test reports summarizing test activities.

stem: Which of the following test tasks is NOT part of the main test activity 'test completion' in the testing process?
options: Creating the product backlog items or change requests for unresolved defects
Archiving the testware that may be useful in the future
Reprioritizing tests when an identified risk becomes an issue
Communicate a test completion report to the stakeholders

stem: Which of the following statements about Acceptance Test-Driven Development (ATDD) is true?
options: ATDD is a "test-first" approach where a test automation framework provides drafts of tests for developers, and these drafts can then be refined into executable test scripts
ATDD is a development approach where test cases are written collectively with stakeholders once the product is ready for acceptance testing
ATDD tests belong to quadrant four (Q4) and are higher-level tests than system tests
In ATDD, acceptance criteria can be turned into acceptance tests to drive the development of the related software

stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical responsibility of the Facilitator?
options: Managing time during review meetings
Ensuring a respectful and open environment for discussion
Making the final decision on whether a work product is accepted
Mediating disagreements between reviewers

stem:
You are testing a PIN validator, which accepts valid PINs and rejects invalid PINs. A PIN is a sequence of digits. A PIN is valid if it consists of four digits, at least two of which are different. You have identified the following valid equivalence partitions:

Variable: PIN code length

  • The partition "length correct" - four-digit PINs
  • The partition "length incorrect(too short)" - PINs with length shorter than 4
  • The partition "length incorrect(too long)" - PINs with length longer than 4

Variable: Number of different digits

  • The partition "number of different digits correct" - PINs with at least two different digits
  • The partition "number of different digits incorrect" - PINs with all digits being the same

Which of the following is a MINIMUM set of input test data that covers all identified equivalence partitions?
Which of the following provides the definition of the term "risk analysis"?

The identification of all work products affected by a change, including an estimate of the resources needed to accomplish the change
The activity that identifies test conditions by analyzing the test basis
The overall process of risk identification and risk assessment

stem: What testware is typically created as output from the test design activity?

Test cases, test charters, test data, coverage items, and test environment requirements

Test cases, test charters, coverage items, test data requirements and test environment requirements

stem: Which of the following is a typical benefit of applying white-box testing techniques?
options: The entire software implementation can't be taken into account during testing, only small components or integrations
White-box testing allows for comprehensive testing of the entire software implementation without access to the source code and need to understand the internal workings of the application
If the software does not implement one or more requirements, white box testing may not detect the resulting defects of omission
White-box techniques are well suited to reviewing code that is not yet ready for execution, as well as pseudocode and other high-level or top-down logic which can be modeled with a control flow graph

stem: Which of the following statements about test completion reports is TRUE?
options: They only include information about successful test cases
They should not mention any deviations from the original test plan
They summarize the overall testing effort and evaluate product quality
They are primarily used to track daily testing activities

stem:
You are testing a user story with three acceptance criteria: AC1, AC2 and AC3. AC1 is covered by test case TC1, AC2 by TC2, and AC3 by TC3. The test execution history had three test runs on three consecutive versions of the software (table with test runs 1-9 showing pass/fail results). Tests are repeated once you are informed that all defects found in the test run are corrected and a new version of the software is available.

Which of the above tests are executed as regression tests?
options: Only 3, 6, 8
Only 6, 9

stem: You are working on a project to develop a system to analyze driving test results. You have been asked to design test cases based on the given decision table. Which of the following test cases represents a situation that can happen in real life, and is missing in the above decision table?
options: A candidate who passed both theoretical and practical exams on the second attempt
A candidate who failed both theoretical and practical exams on the first attempt
A candidate who passed the theoretical exam on the first attempt but failed the practical exam
A candidate who passed the theoretical exam on the second attempt but failed the practical exam

stem: Which of the following is NOT a valid test objective?
options: Validating whether the test object is complete and works as expected by the stakeholders
To ensure the test environment is identical to the production environment in every detail
Verifying that a test object complies with contractual, legal, and regulatory requirements
Reducing the level of risk of inadequate software quality
explanation: - Evaluating work products such as requirements, user stories, designs, and code - Triggering failures and finding defects - Ensuring required coverage of a test object - Reducing the level of risk of inadequate software quality - Verifying whether specified requirements have been fulfilled - Verifying that a test object complies with contractual, legal, and regulatory requirements - Providing information to stakeholders to allow them to make informed decisions - Building confidence in the quality of the test object - Validating whether the test object is complete and works as expected by the stakeholders Ensuring the test environment is identical to production in every detail is not a test objective.

stem: According to the ISTQB Glossary, what is a test approach?
options: The implementation of the test strategy for a specific project
Documentation aligned with the test policy that describes the generic requirements for testing and details how to perform testing within an organization
Documentation describing the test objectives to be achieved and the means and the schedule for achieving them, organized to coordinate testing activities
The set of interrelated activities comprising test planning, test monitoring and control, test analysis, test design, test implementation, test execution, and test completion

stem: Why is it important to regularly update a testing checklist?
options: To adjust for changes in team members

stem: Consider the user story: "As a customer, I want to search for products, so that I can find what I need." Which of the following acceptance criteria would be the MOST important to include?

stem: During the testing phase, testers observe a behavior in the software that appears inconsistent or unintended based on their understanding of the requirements. They report this behavior as a bug. When developers investigate the reported issue, they start to argue that the observed behavior is intentional and aligns with the specifications. options: Agree with the developer who wrote the code and close the defect report or change its priority to a minor
Immediately set up a meeting with the product owner, technical manager, other developers, and the test lead to determine whether it is a bug or a feature

stem:
Consider the following test characteristics (1-4) and Agile testing quadrants (A-D):

  • These tests are designed from the business perspective and may involve the use of techniques such as ATDD and BDD
  • These tests are usually manual tests, as they are both difficult to automate and require user and tester experience and innovation

A. Agile testing quadrant Q1: technology facing, supporting the development team

B. Agile testing quadrant Q2: business facing, supporting the development team

How do the following test categories map onto the agile testing quadrants?

Your team uses planning poker to estimate the test effort for a newly required feature.

Given the user story: "As a user, I want to be able to send and receive messages easily on the platform to communicate with other users in a convenient and efficient manner"

  • Each estimator has a deck of cards with values similar to the Fibonacci sequence (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21)
  • If someone considers a user story big, they assign an estimate of 100

Two iterations of the planning poker sessions have occurred:

During the first iteration:

  • Scrum master: 13
  • Developer: 21
  • Tester: 100

During the second iteration:

  • Scrum master: 21
  • Developer: 100
  • Tester: 100

What is the best outcome for this planning poker session, assuming the time limit of the planning poker sessions for estimating this story has been reached?
options: Since the time limit has been reached, there is no possibility of another planning poker session. The Scrum master selects 21 since this is the highest valid estimated value

Since the difference is still too large, another planning poker session has to be forced. Prior to the third session, the Developers and the tester should change their scores to the suitable as their scores are too high
The members vote if another iteration has to proceed or not. If not, then the team breaks down the user story into multiple smaller stories

stem: Which of the following is the benefit of Agile software development?

Manual testing becomes outdated and redundant with the automation of regression test suites, the adoption of a shift-left approach, and the implementation of DevOps methodologies
Integrating testing as a core component and the primary phase of software development, exemplified by practices like TDD, BDD, and ATDD

stem: What is the primary purpose of risk monitoring in product risk analysis?

stem:
A tester discovers a defect where the application fails to calculate the correct total price for items in a shopping cart. Which of the following items would be most helpful in the defect report for the development team?

i. List of all failed test cases in the test run

ii. Expected total price and the incorrect total price displayed

iii. Documented lessons learned

v. Screenshots of each step of the checkout process

vi. List of all team members involved in the project
options: ii, iv, v
i, ii, v
ii, iv, vi
i, iv, vi
explanation: - Unique identifier - Title with a short summary - Date when the anomaly was observed, issuing organization, and author, including their role - Identification of the test object and test environment - Context of the defect - Description of the failure, the steps that detected the anomaly, and any relevant test logs, database dumps, screenshots, or recordings - Expected results and actual results - Severity - Priority - Status - References

stem:
Consider the following user story:

Acceptance Criteria:

  • AC2: Users can apply one of the following coupon codes at checkout: "Saver5" for a 5% discount, "Super10" for a 10% discount, "Mega15" for a 15% discount
  • AC3: If a user purchases exactly 5 products, a 'Bulk Buy Discount' of 10% is automatically applied to their order
